# Refactor guard: sync split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Position in chain:** 1 of 6 — blocks every extraction child.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/sync.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely, no existing test file changes, and no reviewer
has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC2/AC3/AC4/AC1 require an unchanged public surface at `./sync.js`, an
unmodified test suite, an acyclic import graph, and no file above 1,000 lines.
Nothing in the root package enforces any of that today: there is no
`madge`/`dependency-cruiser`, the repo-wide file-size guard
(WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL) is still `idea`, and the only existing split guards are
the `packages/herdr` ones (`downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`,
`index.split-guard.test.ts`) which are scoped to that package. This child
builds the enforcement first, mirroring the guard child of the sibling
decomposition (WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E for `downtime-worker.ts`) and the
`packages/shared` equivalent (WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-26, `dev` @ `f39b2463`-era tree):

- `src/sync.ts` — 1,867 lines, **34 exports = 25 value exports (functions and
  one `const`) + 9 type exports (8 `interface` + 1 `type` alias)**. (The parent
  description's "23 functions/consts + 11 interfaces/types" split is corrected
  here; the total of 34 is unchanged.)
- 10 source files import from `./sync.js` / `../sync.js`: `src/database.ts`,
  `src/logging.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/index.ts`,
  `src/commands/{sync,init,migrate,helpers,doctor,delete}.ts`.
- 11 test files import from `../src/sync.js` (two of them via dynamic
  `await import()`): `sync.test.ts`, `sync-whitelist.test.ts`,
  `sync-author-gate.test.ts`, `sync-worktree.test.ts`,
  `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `sync-regression-guard.test.ts`,
  `sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`,
  `sync-audit-results.test.ts`, `unit/audit-sync-monotonic.test.ts`,
  `cli/git-mock-roundtrip.test.ts`.
- 1 internal importer: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` imports `type { MergeOptions }`
  from `'../sync.js'` — the only known would-be cycle, to be re-pointed at
  `src/sync/types.ts` by child 2.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure — `src/sync.ts` and every `src/sync*.ts` / `src/sync/**/*.ts` module — is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   Verified mechanically (`wc -l`) and recorded in the completion comment, driven
   by an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains only `'sync.ts'` and
   is asserted to only ever shrink (remain a subset of the plan-time list).
2. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The committed baseline `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` records the 34
   symbol names (25 value + 9 type, flagged separately) plus provenance
   (generation command, source commit, timestamp), and a machine gate fails the
   suite when any one is lost — value exports resolvable at runtime, type
   exports present in the emitted declaration.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   The guard's completion evidence shows zero diffs across the 77 existing test
   files; any accidental behavioural delta is reverted, not "fixed" in place.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic and recorded in the module responsibility table.
   The static import graph of `src/sync.ts` + `src/sync/**/*.ts` contains no
   cycle (no module imports a module that imports it back); after the final child
   no production module under `src/sync/` contains a runtime (value) import of
   `'../sync.js'`. The gate is green now — the single `merge-utils.ts` type-only
   import sits in an explicit allowlist that child 2 removes — and red on any new
   violation.
5. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
   The guard suite itself is documented the same way, so the standard is
   established before the extraction children land.
6. New **additive** test file `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` (vitest) exists
   and passes on the current tree before any production code moves; no existing
   test file is modified.
7. **Negative proofs.** Each of the three gates is proven to fail on a
   deliberately broken input (synthetic >1,000-line module, dropped export,
   synthetic import cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
8. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes via the test skill, and `npm run build` — for this child, `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes including the
   new guard suite, and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Minimal implementation

1. Generate the baseline from `src/sync.ts` (regex-free, TypeScript compiler
   API or `tsc`-emitted `.d.ts` after `npm run build`) — normalise, sort,
   flag value-vs-type, and write JSON with provenance fields.
2. Write `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` with one named `it()` per gate
   (surface, size + allowlist, cycle/barrel, negative proofs) so failures are
   legible.
3. Put the pure predicates (parse module → imports/exports; build graph; find
   cycles) in `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` so the negative-proof tests can
   feed them synthetic sources without touching the tree.
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` and `TYPE_ONLY_BARREL_ALLOWLIST` so child 2 and
   child 6 can shrink them by one line each.
5. Record the baseline generation command in the file header, then run
   `/skill:test` (changed scope) and `npm run build` and paste both outcomes in
   a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — new guard suite.
- `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` — new pure gate predicates/scanners.
- `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` — new frozen export baseline.
- `src/sync.ts` — read-only in this child (no edits).
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — read-only in this child (allowlisted).

## Dependencies

None — first child. Every extraction child (2–6) is blocked by this one.

## Constraints

- Move-only / additive: production code and existing tests are untouched.
- Do not add `madge`, `dependency-cruiser` or any new runtime/dev dependency —
  graph and size checks are plain TypeScript.
- No edits to the `packages/herdr` split guards and no relocation of their
  `scan.ts`; this guard is root-package-scoped. Sharing a common scanner with
  the other packages is deliberately out of scope (would widen blast radius).
- A repo-wide file-size guard remains WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL; this guard covers
  only `sync.ts` and `sync/`.

## Deliverables

Frozen export baseline, guard suite + scanners, negative proofs, green
`/skill:test` (changed scope) and green `npm run build` recorded in a comment.

## Problem

The test-run cache (`skill/test_cache.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

**Implementation repository:** the cache code lives in the **SorraAgents** skills repo. This item is tracked in the ContextHub worklog (where it was discovered); all paths below are relative to the SorraAgents repo root.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state()`, `run_cached()`, `lookup()`, `store()`, `query_cached()`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `--scope changed`, `--summary`, `[cached]` marker in non-JSON output
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — existing cache-fingerprint unit tests
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` — existing run_tests cache-integration tests
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — the test-skill cache contract documentation

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Verified context (checked while planning, 2026-10-30)

- **Content-sensitive fingerprinting already shipped.** SA-0MVGKZN8C006YNV8 (commit `b51609654`, 2026-10-20) made `compute_git_state()` hash HEAD **plus the content of every path** in `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`. Symptom 1 was observed on 2026-10-26, *after* that fix — so the residual stale hit is **not** the already-fixed content-hash gap; the implementer must reproduce it and find the path that bypasses or mis-times the fingerprint.
- **Symptom 2 has an identified mechanism.** `run_cached()` computes `git_state` **before** the run and stores the entry under that pre-run state, so any transient dirty state at run start (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) keys an entry that a clean checkout at the same HEAD can never query again.
- **The `[cached]` marker already exists** in non-JSON run output (SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY, 2026-08-06), so cache visibility is a regression-guard requirement rather than new behaviour.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Content-only edits invalidate: editing only the contents of an already-modified (dirty) file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group, proven by a regression test (run A → edit an already-dirty file → run B) that fails against the un-fixed code and passes after the fix.
- AC2 — Post-run queryability: immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full` completes, `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` from a clean checkout at the same HEAD reports the stored entry instead of `missing`, covered by a regression test.
- AC3 — Cache visibility guarded: a cache-served result remains marked `[cached]` in non-JSON output and that marker is covered by a regression test so it cannot silently regress.
- AC4 — Root cause recorded: the mechanism behind each symptom is recorded on this item as a comment before the fix lands, and both regression tests are demonstrated RED against the pre-fix code and GREEN afterwards.
- AC5 — Docs: `skill/test/SKILL.md` states that runs whose result proves RED/GREEN (or supplies evidence an audit consumes) must use `--no-cache`.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Changing the cache key/namespace model (tree fingerprints, worktree/main-checkout unification) — tracked by SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB and SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V. This item must not duplicate or block those.

## Risky assumptions

- The residual stale hit (symptom 1) is fixable without changing the fingerprint contract. If reproduction shows it needs the tree-fingerprint binding, stop, record the finding on SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB, and re-scope this item instead of expanding it.
- `--scope changed` runs are keyed per-command through `run_cached()`, so a content edit must change the key; if it does not, the defect is in the changed-scope command/file-list derivation rather than in the fingerprint.

## Related work

- SA-0MVGKZN8C006YNV8 (completed) — content-based git-state fingerprint; partial overlap with AC1's original premise.
- SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB (blocked) — tree-fingerprint cache binding for the finish gate.
- SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V (open) — unify the test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout.
- WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (completed) — discovery session.

## OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking)

- OPEN QUESTION for the producer: AC3 keeps today's per-suite `[cached]` marker; is that enough of a signal, or should a cached run also be surfaced at the run/JSON summary level (e.g. `cached_suites`)? Non-blocking — AC3 guards existing behaviour with a test either way.
- OPEN QUESTION for the producer: should the symptom-2 fix also make previously orphaned entries discoverable (re-key on demand), or is preventing orphaned entries (store under a state the operator can reproduce) sufficient? Non-blocking — AC2 only requires that newly stored entries are queryable.

# Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble shared by gitPushDataFileToBranch and rewriteAndForcePushDataFile

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 (*Extract sync worktree, remote-fetch and push modules*, sync split, child 5 of 6) — filed under that item's constraint that known awkwardness in this region is recorded as a work item rather than refactored inline.

## Problem statement

`src/sync/push.ts` contains two public push paths — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental commit on the existing data-ref history) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (fresh orphan commit force-pushed over a polluted history) — and each carries its own near-identical copy of the same preamble: cross-project guard, `refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/` safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, repo-root/relative-path resolution, data-file existence check, `withTempWorktree(...)`, and the force-add / `diff --cached` / commit staging dance. A fix to any one of those steps (a guard message, a path-handling bug, an empty-stage policy) must currently be made twice and can silently drift.

## Users

- **Maintainer of the sync layer** — "As a maintainer, I want the shared preamble in one private helper so a guard or path-handling fix applies to both push paths, and each public function reads as its actual difference (empty-stage policy + push mode)."
- **Reviewer of a sync change** — "As a reviewer, I want to see one copy of each guard so I can verify a safety change without diffing two near-identical blocks."
- **Operator running `wl sync` / `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push`** — indirect: both paths keep their current observable behaviour (silent no-op vs hard failure) exactly.

## Existing state

- `gitPushDataFileToBranch(repoDataFilePath, commitMessage, target): Promise<void>` — shared steps, then cleans foreign tracked files from the data branch, copies the JSONL, `add -f`, `diff --cached`, **silently returns** when nothing is staged, commits, then `git push --no-verify <remote> HEAD:<ref>`.
- `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile(repoDataFilePath, commitMessage, target): Promise<string>` — same shared steps (minus the foreign-file cleanup), **throws `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref`** when nothing is staged, commits, then `git push --force --no-verify`, then reads `rev-parse HEAD` inside the worktree callback (the returned `tipSha`), updates the local remote-tracking ref, and returns the SHA.
- Differences that must survive the refactor: (a) empty-stage policy `silent return` vs `throw`; (b) existence check `silent return` vs `throw Worklog data file not found: …`; (c) safety-guard message — the incremental path appends the hint `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 to bypass the pre-push hook.`, the rewrite path does not; (d) `withTempWorktree` option `forceOrphan: true` only on the rewrite path; (e) push flags `--no-verify` vs `--force --no-verify`; (f) only the rewrite path returns a value (the new tip SHA) and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` afterwards.
- Current sizes: `src/sync/push.ts` 199 lines, `src/sync.ts` (barrel) 100 lines — both far below the 1,000-line ceiling; this item is about removing duplication, not about the ceiling.
- Structural gate already in place: `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` parses the module tree and asserts the frozen barrel surface (`tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json`, 34 symbols), the ≤ 1,000-line ceiling and an acyclic import graph. A private helper inside `push.ts` changes none of those, so this gate must stay green **without** re-baselining.
- Test coverage today: `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` covers orphan-branch creation, target validation and the `--no-verify` source grep; `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` covers the happy-path rewrite, the refs safety rejection, the missing-file throw and sequential reentrancy. **Not covered:** the incremental path's silent no-op on an empty stage, and the rewrite path's `Nothing staged for the rewrite` throw — i.e. exactly the two policies that distinguish the paths and are most at risk in a dedupe refactor.

## Desired change

Introduce one private helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) that owns the shared preamble and delegates the mode-specific tail to a callback:

- Guard + resolve: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo(repoDataFilePath)`, the `refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/` rejection, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` / `path.resolve()` and the existence check.
- Materialise: `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, ..., { forceOrphan })`, `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- Empty-stage policy as an explicit option (`'skip' | 'throw'`) — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op without invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing message.
- Commit, then invoke the caller's `run` with the worktree context (`worktreePath`, `relativePath`, escaped forms) so each caller performs only its own push (`--no-verify` vs `--force --no-verify`) and, for the rewrite path, reads `rev-parse HEAD`.
- The safety-guard workaround hint is a parameter so both messages stay byte-identical to today.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper → do their mode-specific push (and, for rewrite, update the tracking ref + return the SHA).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
2. **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
3. **Existing suites pass and the grep assertion is not weakened.** `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` and `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` pass unchanged in intent; if the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion still exists it is re-pointed (and still asserts the same property) rather than deleted or loosened — if WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z has already replaced it with a behavioural test, no re-point is needed and this clause is satisfied trivially.
4. **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
5. **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
6. **Testing / validation criterion.** The two currently-uncovered policies in AC2(c) and AC2(d) each gain at least one meaningful test that fails if the policy is swapped between the two paths (negative proof, not just a happy-path assertion).
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature, no behavioural, no error-message change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` surface is unchanged.
- Helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts` — `src/sync/worktree.ts` remains a generic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts` (see Risks).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; the full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy parameter applied to both paths would silently turn the rewrite path's hard failure into a no-op (publishing nothing while reporting success) or turn a routine no-change sync into an error. Mitigation: AC2(c)/AC6 tests pin both directions.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two safety-guard messages would drop the `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where it does not belong). Mitigation: hint is an explicit parameter; AC2(a) asserts the exact text.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }` through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path would fetch the polluted ref again (the exact bug the split fixed). Mitigation: `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` rewrites a seeded polluted remote and asserts foreign items are gone.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing; the helper's generic return (`Promise<T | undefined>`) must stay honest so callers cannot silently drop the SHA. Mitigation: rewrite path throws on `undefined` or types the helper with a non-optional return for the `'throw'` policy.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The read paths in `src/sync/remote.ts` repeat the same `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` + `git rev-parse --git-dir` + repo-root resolution trio. That is a separate opportunity: record it as a linked follow-up work item, do not absorb it here.
- **Assumption:** the helper lives in `push.ts` rather than `worktree.ts` (see Appendix Q1); **assumption:** the empty-stage policy remains path-specific rather than unified (Q2); **assumption:** the source-grep assertion is left to WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z if that lands first (Q3).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync/push.ts` — Needs the new private `withDataFileInTempWorktree` helper; both public functions rewritten on top of it; module header updated.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only (unchanged): supplies `withTempWorktree`, `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): supplies `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRelativePath`.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `getRemoteTrackingRef` used by the rewrite path's post-push bookkeeping.
- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify exports are byte-identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Add the incremental-path policy tests (silent no-op on empty stage, silent no-op on missing file); re-point the `--no-verify` grep if it still exists.
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Add the empty-stage `Nothing staged for the rewrite` test; keep the refs-rejection and missing-file tests.
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green): structural gates over the module tree; `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` must not be regenerated.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Update the `src/sync/push.ts` row if the module's description (helper present) changes.

## Related work

Curated from repo/worklog search plus the `find-related` run for this item (its raw keyword report was reviewed but is transient; the items that matter are listed below and the rest were keyword noise):

- **WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1** — *Extract sync worktree, remote-fetch and push modules* (open, `plan_complete`, high). The split that created `src/sync/push.ts`; this item's outbound dependency and the source of the duplication.
- **WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z** — *Replace the source-grep push assertion in tests/sync-worktree.test.ts with a behavioural test* (open, low). Overlaps AC3: it removes the grep assertion this item would otherwise have to re-point.
- **WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ** — *Refactor: decompose src/sync.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines)* (open). The parent epic of the sync decomposition.
- **WL-0MVP9SEJZ000KWXJ** — *Finalise sync barrel, documentation and close-out* (completed). Landed the barrel/`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` layout this item must keep in sync.
- **WL-0MSGNDSCR0096MCR** — *wl sync fails: duplicate 'git worktree add' in withTempWorktree* (completed). Prior bug in exactly this worktree path; the behaviour must not regress.
- **Potentially related docs:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (§ sync module map and "where to change what" table), `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (dev-facing orientation to the sync layout, including the worktree-isolation rules the helper must preserve), `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (why the incremental path commits onto existing ref history instead of forcing).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers below record the agent's research plus the recommended option that was applied pending producer override (per the interview contract, the recommendation is advisory and the operator may change it).

- **Q1 — Where should the shared helper live: private in `src/sync/push.ts`, or exported from `src/sync/worktree.ts`?**

Evidence: `grep -rn "gitPushDataFileToBranch|rewriteAndForcePushDataFile" src/` shows the only callers are `src/sync/push.ts` (definitions), the barrel, and three consumers that go through the barrel; `worktree.ts` is imported by `remote.ts` and `push.ts` and documents itself as data-file-agnostic. ## Problem

`tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` ("push command uses --no-verify to avoid recursive pre-push hook") reads production source and greps for the literal push command line. That is anti-pattern #1 in the shared Test Writing Guidelines (grep source instead of asserting behaviour): it couples the test to a file path and a literal command string, so any legitimate move (as in the sync split) or message reformat breaks it, while a real regression in push behaviour would not necessarily be caught.

Child 5 re-pointed the grep from `src/sync.ts` to `src/sync/push.ts` (assertions unchanged) to keep the gate green — a stop-gap, not a fix.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test to prove the observable behaviour — that pushes performed by the sync push paths bypass the pre-push hook — without grepping source text.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The test drives `gitPushDataFileToBranch` through the existing git mock (which already traces invocations) and asserts the recorded push invocation contains `--no-verify` (and, for the rewrite path, `--force --no-verify`).
2. No `readFileSync` of production source remains in the test for this behaviour.
3. The test fails if `--no-verify` is removed from either push command (negative proof), and passes on the current tree.
4. Only `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (plus mock assertions if required) changes; no production behaviour change; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.

- Related: WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 re-pointed the assertion; this item removes the anti-pattern.

Fix stale packages/herdr/package-lock.json drift that fails the test-skill live-repo guard

Discovered during WL-0MVOBP6K0007574C (extract dependency and comment modules).

## Problem

`packages/herdr/package.json` declares a root `bin` entry
(`worklog-pane-close` -> `dist/pane-close-cli.js`) and a `postinstall` script,
but the committed `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` (last touched
2026-08-11, WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4) predates both. Any `npm ci`/`npm install` in
that package rewrites the lockfile with `hasInstallScript: true` and the root
`bin` block.

`tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` executes `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
(cwd = repo root), which runs `npm ci` inside `packages/herdr`. The rewritten
lockfile is therefore a mutation of a guarded checkout made during a test run,
so the test skill's live-repo guard fails the run:

```
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for <repo>.
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/package-lock.json
```

Every test in the suite passes (281 files / 4,113 tests, exit 0) — only the run
verdict is failed. Consequences:

- The per-repo test cache can never hold a green full-suite entry for HEAD, so
  the audit skill cannot auto-verify execution-dependent ACs (F3 re-executes and
  fails the same way).
- Each full-suite run leaves the main checkout dirty.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` is regenerated (`npm install` in
   `packages/herdr`) and committed so it matches `package.json`'s `bin` and
   `postinstall`.
2. A full-suite run (`run_tests.py --scope full`) at that commit reports
   `success: true` with no `live_repo_mutation` field, and leaves
   `git status` clean.
3. `npm run build` and `npm ci` in `packages/herdr` produce no further lockfile
   diff.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/package-lock.json`
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — read-only
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` — read-only (reproduction)

## Constraint

Lockfile-only change; do not alter `package.json` or the install script.

discovered-from:WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V

## Goal

**As** an operator running several worklog roots on one machine, **I want** the downtime leader to know about a root even when no herdr instance happens to be running in it, **so that** a root with dispatchable work is never invisible to the dispatcher.

## Problem

The dispatcher's candidate universe is derived from **live instances**, not registered roots:

- `computeMostImportantItem` runs per instance and is called by `runCoordinationCheckIn`; only a running herdr instance in a root writes a coordination entry (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts:145`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:928+`).
- The leader's only cross-root reach is the offer list plus one own-backlog fallback hard-scoped to `opts.cwd` (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:801-880`, AC2 of WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24).

Measured 2026-10-27T21:55Z: `ContextHub` has **9 of 30** window items dispatchable (`WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ`, `WL-0MNM7EVJG0097Y44`, `WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND`, six refactor items, …), and **zero** coordination entries, because no herdr instance is running in that root. Its per-worklog `downtime-coordination.json` is `{"version":1,"entries":[]}`. The machine-wide file holds only `tce-the-rising` entries.

Leadership rotation cannot fix this: the empty-leader hand-off (`WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A`) hands off to *a peer*, and there is no peer in that root to hand off to.

## Why this is separate from `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V`

It is a different problem class — **root discovery**, not dispatcher gating. Fixing the audit-tier budget or adding attribution would not make a root with no open pane reachable. Conversely, a root sweep would not have fixed `AI_Hell` (all items held) or `tce-the-rising` (audit tier unreachable).

## Options (to evaluate at intake)

- **O1 — Registered roots.** An explicit config list (e.g. `downtimeWorklogRoots`), or discovery by scanning a parent directory for `.worklog/worklog.db`. The leader sweeps registered roots round-robin via `getHerdrListHead(root, window)` and applies the same sequential filter chain. Note `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` still exists with a cursor (the retired-by-WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 helpers), so the cursor machinery is partly present.
- **O2 — Per-root offers from a single instance.** One instance offers on behalf of a set of roots. Cheaper than O1 but reintroduces "who offers which root" ownership questions.
- **O3 — Hardware/heartbeat registry.** Instances publish liveness per root so the leader can distinguish "no instance" from "instance offered nothing". Overlaps with the stale-entry problem (see below).

## Related observation

Coordination entries never expire: `pruneStaleEntries` is a deliberate no-op (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts:366`, WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P), and `hasPeerOffer` (`coordination.ts:350`) only checks `instanceId !== self && workItemId.length > 0`. During the 2026-10-27 investigation the dead instance `b4365ff1` (lastUpdated `2026-10-27T14:30:20Z`, 7+ hours stale) still counted as a live peer. The predicate is documented as "conservative… never a starvation", which was sound when entries expired; with expiry retired it no longer is. Any solution here should also decide whether a stale entry should make the leader *more* willing to sweep.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A root with dispatchable work but **no running herdr instance** is reachable by the leader, and work from it is dispatched. Verified live on `ContextHub` (currently 9 dispatchable, 0 offers).
- AC2: `AI_Hell`-style gated roots are still not dispatched — a sweep must not bypass any existing safety gate (`assignee` hold, producer-review, code-freeze, freshness, caps, slot minimums, in-flight, review-queue). Gates remain sequential filters.
- AC3: The canonical ranking contract is preserved: a sweep is a bounded **window** over registered roots using the same `getHerdrListHead` path, never a second ranking.
- AC4: Fairness: no single root can monopolise the leader (a bounded per-root share or round-robin cursor), demonstrated by a multi-root test with two roots each holding dispatchable work.
- AC5: Fail-open: an unreadable/missing root in the registry is skipped without a strike, and never crashes the tick.
- AC6: Fail-safe: an empty or unresolvable registry leaves today's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.
- AC7: The stale-coordination-entry question above is explicitly resolved (either entries gain a heartbeat, or `hasPeerOffer` is made liveness-aware) with the decision recorded on this item.
- AC8: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the root-discovery model and how it composes with the offer list.

## Constraints

- Must not reinstate the unconditional non-critical window widening superseded by WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9.
- Must not require a running pane per root (that is the bug being fixed).
- Config schema additions need clamping/validation consistent with `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.

# Pin push-path policy divergence with tests

Test-first safety net for WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push
preamble shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`*).

**No production code changes in this child.** It adds the tests that must be
green **before** `src/sync/push.ts` is refactored, so the dedupe is verified
against pinned behaviour instead of against a re-read of the same code.

## Why

The two push paths deliberately diverge on two policies, and **neither
divergent policy is covered by a test today**:

| Policy | `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) | `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (rewrite) |
|---|---|---|
| Empty stage (`diff --cached` names nothing) | returns silently | throws `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` |
| Data file missing | returns silently | throws `Worklog data file not found: …` |

Those are exactly the policies a shared helper can silently unify. Each needs a
**negative-proof** test: one that fails if the policy is swapped between the two
paths (an assertion that the other path's behaviour does *not* occur).

Two further divergences must also be pinned byte-exactly:

- the safety-guard message — the incremental path appends
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 to bypass the pre-push hook.`, the rewrite path
  does not;
- the push flags — `--no-verify` (incremental) vs `--force --no-verify`
  (rewrite).

## Scope — tests only

### `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (incremental path; mock-`git` driven today)

- **Empty stage** resolves without error and performs no push (no `push` call
  in the mock trace / no ref created on the fake remote).
- **Missing data file** (path inside the repo, file absent) resolves without
  error — i.e. it does **not** throw `Worklog data file not found`.
- **`refs/tags/*` rejection** asserts today's exact message text, including the
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint.
- **Cross-project guard** still fires when the data file lives in a different
  git repository than the process cwd.
- **Re-point the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion** (currently
  `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts:286-305`): it must keep asserting "no push line
  in `src/sync/push.ts` lacks `--no-verify`" and "a `push --no-verify` line
  exists". Re-pointed, **not deleted or loosened**. The sibling that would
  delete it (WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z) is still at `idea`, so this item owns the
  re-point.

### `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` (rewrite path; real-`git` driven)

- **Empty stage** rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite` — and does
  **not** resolve.
- **`refs/heads/*` rejection** asserts today's exact message text and asserts
  the message does **not** carry the `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` hint.
- **`--force`** is used: the remote ref is replaced rather than fast-forwarded.
- Keep the existing missing-file, refs-rejection and reentrancy tests unchanged
  in intent.

## Implementation notes

- The mock git (`tests/cli/mock-bin/git`) has **no `diff` handler**: its
  fallback prints the argv to stdout, which makes `diff --cached` look
  non-empty and hides the empty-stage branch. For the incremental empty-stage
  test, prefer a **real-`git`** test in the style of
  `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — seed a bare remote whose
  `refs/worklog/data` already contains byte-identical JSONL, then call
  `gitPushDataFileToBranch` with the same bytes so the copy stages nothing. If
  the mock must gain a `diff` case instead, gate it behind an env var so
  existing suites are unaffected.
- The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup means a seeded ref should
  contain only the data file, or the cleanup will stage deletions.
- Do not weaken an existing assertion to make a new test pass; if a test cannot
  be expressed behaviourally, record an open question rather than grep source.

## Constraints

- No production-code edits (`src/**`).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - **Empty stage (negative proof)** — the incremental path resolves without error and performs no push; an added test fails if the incremental path starts throwing.
  - **Empty stage (negative proof)** — the rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref`; an added test fails if the rewrite path starts resolving.
  - **Missing data file (negative proof)** — the incremental path resolves (no throw) and the rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; each assertion fails if the policies are swapped.
  - **(a) Refs rejection** — `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` rejected on both paths with today's exact text, including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only.
  - **(b) Cross-project guard** — still fires on both paths when the data file belongs to a different git repository.
  - **(e) Push flags** — `--no-verify` on the incremental path; `--force --no-verify` on the rewrite path.

- **Existing suites pass and the grep assertion is not weakened.** `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` and `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` pass unchanged in intent; if the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion still exists it is re-pointed (and still asserts the same property) rather than deleted or loosened — if WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z has already replaced it with a behavioural test, no re-point is needed and this clause is satisfied trivially.
  - The `--no-verify` source-grep assertion in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (currently ~:286-305) is re-pointed so it still asserts 'no push line in `src/sync/push.ts` lacks `--no-verify`' — re-pointed, not deleted or loosened. Sibling WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z (which would delete it) is still at `idea`.
  - `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` passes unchanged in intent.

- **Testing / validation criterion.** The two currently-uncovered policies in AC2(c) and AC2(d) each gain at least one meaningful test that fails if the policy is swapped between the two paths (negative proof, not just a happy-path assertion).
  - The incremental empty-stage and the rewrite empty-stage tests each fail if the policy is swapped between the two paths; likewise the two missing-file tests.
  - Every new and re-pointed test passes against the **current, pre-refactor** implementation.
  - `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.

## Key Files

- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — incremental-path policy tests and the
  `--no-verify` grep re-point.
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — rewrite-path empty-stage test, exact
  guard-message assertions, explicit `--force` assertion.
- `src/sync/push.ts` — Read only (unchanged): the implementation these tests
  pin.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only: supplies the cross-project guard the
  guard test exercises.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only: supplies `withTempWorktree`, used by the
  real-`git` incremental test.

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).
  - The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback; the rewrite path still returns the new tip SHA and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
  - Duplicate-block inspection: none of the ten preamble steps appears twice.

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - The sibling's tests (empty-stage, missing-file, refs messages, cross-project guard, push flags) pass unchanged and green after the refactor.
  - `{ forceOrphan: true }` is threaded to `withTempWorktree` on the rewrite path only; the pre-push hint appears on the incremental path only; the rewrite path cannot silently drop the tip SHA.

## Goal

Invert the skip-on-skew policy in the audit-fingerprint parity test so a fingerprint-schema skew between the installed audit skill and this CLI **fails** — loudly — instead of silently skipping. Environment unavailability stays a skip. Covers parent AC1 + AC2 + AC3 (contract side).

Discovered-from: WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y (bug: false-stale audit badge, LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: a contract declaring a schema different from `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` (ahead or behind) yields a **FAIL** outcome whose actionable message names the installed schema, the expected schema, the scripts directory, and the remediation (reinstall via `scripts/install_pi.sh` or set `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS`).
- AC2: a contract declaring **no schema** (pre-v2 install) yields a **FAIL** outcome naming the installed path and the schema-constant lookup — an undeclared schema cannot be proven compatible (fail-safe). A unit test documents the observed failure: a schema-1-format Python report's stored fingerprint never matches the schema-2 `computeContentFingerprint` for the same title/description.
- AC3: genuine environment unavailability stays a **SKIP** with the existing reason: no scripts dir, no `python3`, or unimportable `_compute_content_fingerprint` (CI without the agent framework stays green).
- AC4: the two existing 'skips when the helper is ahead or behind' tests are inverted to fail, an undeclared-schema failure case is added, and the alive parity digest comparison still runs when the contract outcome is OK. The suite therefore goes **red** on a skewed host by design.
- AC5: the probe/evaluation logic is deterministic and unit-testable with injected contracts (no live `python3` needed in unit tests); env-missing cases keep their descriptive skip reasons.
- AC6: the parity test file header docstring states the new fail-on-skew contract (removes the old skip-on-skew rationale; full doc update is the sibling docs child).
Parent AC coverage (restated for traceability — WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y):

- AC-P1: `evaluateInstalledContract` no longer treats a schema skew as a silent skip — any declared schema different from the expected one fails.
- AC-P2: a helper that declares no schema at all (pre-v2 install) is treated as skew and fails.
- AC-P3: genuine environment unavailability remains a skip, not a red herring.
- AC-P7: the full test suite passes with the changes. No strictness env gate is added.

## Constraints

- No change to the fingerprint payload or `isAuditFresh` semantics.
- No `AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_PARITY_STRICT` env gate — fail-on-skew is the contract (operator-confirmed option 1A in the parent Appendix).
- AC3 skip path must be preserved verbatim for CI images.

## Key Files

- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — invert skew policy; add undeclared-schema + schema-1-never-matches tests; keep env skips.
- `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` (new) — shared installed-skill probe + outcome model (`ok` | `skip` | `fail`), extracted from the test file so the parity test and the `wl doctor` check reuse one probe (parent risk record: 're-uses the same probe rather than duplicating import logic').

## Minimal Implementation

1. **Tests first:** rewrite the parity-test skew cases to expect FAIL for ahead/behind/undeclared (plus the schema-1-never-matches case) and SKIP for env-missing — confirm they are red against the current skip policy.
2. Extract `findAuditScripts`, `pythonAvailable`, `probeInstalledContract`, `evaluateInstalledContract` into `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts`, returning a discriminated outcome (ok/skip/fail), and wire the test to import it.
3. Map skew (declared ≠ expected) and undeclared schema to a `fail` outcome with the actionable message (installed schema, expected schema, scripts dir, remediation); run the digest parity comparison only on `ok`.
4. Update the test header docstring to the fail-on-skew contract.

## Definition of done

Targeted `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` + `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` tests green via the test skill; no regression in the alive parity check.

## Verification

`wl show WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y --children --json` — parent ACs 1, 2, 3 covered by this child's ACs.

## Dependencies

None.

## Goal

Prove the reported failure mode and its fix with self-contained fixtures: an item whose stored fingerprint came from a **schema-2** audit report is `isAuditFresh`; an item whose stored fingerprint came from a **schema-1** (pre-v2 `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}`) report is not. Covers parent AC5.

Discovered-from: WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y (bug: false-stale audit badge, LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: a test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedSchema2, currentSchema2)` is **true** for identical item content, where `storedSchema2` is computed with the schema-2 payload (the same shape the Python `_compute_content_fingerprint` emits).
- AC2: a test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedSchema1, currentSchema2)` is **false** for the same content, where `storedSchema1` is computed with the pre-v2 payload `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` (schema 1, verified against `git show 213a96b7^:src/audit-fingerprint.ts`) — the false-stale mode this bug reports.
- AC3: the test is fully self-contained (in-memory audit-record fixtures + in-test digest computation; no DB, no git, no Python, no live worklog data) and therefore deterministic — this repo currently has **zero** fingerprint-bearing audits since the 2026-10-23 schema-2 port.
- AC4: a test documents that the mismatch is a *bare string compare* in `isAuditFresh` (no tolerances, no time-gate rescue when both fingerprints are present), so the skew cannot silently resolve itself.
- AC5: test names/header make the intent obvious to a future maintainer ("a schema skew must never read as fresh").
Parent AC coverage (restated for traceability — WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y):

- AC-P5: an end-to-end freshness test proves the reported failure mode and its fix.

## Constraints

- No behavioural change to `isAuditFresh` or the fingerprint payload — the test asserts current behaviour.
- Prefer minimal fixtures: one title/description pair, two stored digests.

## Key Files

- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — add the freshness/skew describe block (parent Key Files places the AC5 test here).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh` reference only; no change.
- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — `computeContentFingerprint` used to build the schema-2 fixture.

## Minimal Implementation

1. In-test helper `schema1Fingerprint({title, description, keyFiles})` reproducing the pre-v2 payload via the existing canonical-JSON/sha256 utilities.
2. Two `it` cases asserting schema-2 → fresh and schema-1 → stale for identical content.
3. One `it` asserting the mismatch cannot be rescued by the 60 s time gate (both fingerprints present ⇒ string compare decides).

## Definition of done

Targeted test file green via the test skill; the two `it` cases fail against the pre-fix expectations (red-then-green proof recorded in the implementation comment).

## Verification

Parent AC5 is satisfied by AC1–AC4 above.

## Dependencies

None (independent of the parity-policy child).

## Goal

Add a **warning-level** `wl doctor` check `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew` that reports the installed vs expected audit-fingerprint schema (and remediation) when the installed skill's schema differs from `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` **or is undeclared**, in both human output and `--json`. Covers parent AC4.

Discovered-from: WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y (bug: false-stale audit badge, LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `wl doctor` on a host whose installed skill declares a schema ≠ 2 (or no schema at all) emits a finding with `checkId: 'audit-fingerprint.schema-skew'`, `severity: 'warning'`, a message naming the installed schema, the expected schema and the remediation, and `context {installedSchema, expectedSchema, scriptsDir, remediation}`; `proposedFix` is null (not auto-fixable) and the run stays non-failing.
- AC2: the same host's `wl doctor --json` output contains exactly that finding (additive to the existing findings array — no change to the top-level `--json` shape).
- AC3: on a host whose installed skill declares schema 2 (this repo's host, verified `audit_runner.py:1222`), no `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew` finding is emitted.
- AC4: graceful skip when `python3`, the scripts dir, or the `audit_runner` import is unavailable: no finding, no error, no failure (mirrors the parity test's AC3).
- AC5: the probe is the **shared** implementation from `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` (contract `ok`/`skip`/`fail` outcome) — the doctor check does not re-implement the Python import probe; one subprocess per `wl doctor` run is acceptable.
- AC6: unit tests cover finding construction from injected contracts (skew, undeclared, ok, env-missing) without spawning Python, plus one CLI test asserting the finding is absent on this schema-2 host.
Parent AC coverage (restated for traceability — WL-0MVOE11V60050Q6Y):

- AC-P4: `wl doctor` gains a warning-level check naming the installed and expected schema.

## Constraints

- Warning only — must never change `wl doctor`'s exit status or break existing workflows.
- Read-only: no DB mutation, no worklog write, no cache introduced (doctor probe cost is noted as a follow-up if it ever matters).
- Do not touch `isAuditFresh` / `wl list` read paths (operator-confirmed option 3A).

## Key Files

- `src/doctor/audit-fingerprint-skew-check.ts` (new) — build the warning finding from the shared installed-contract outcome.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — register the finding in the findings assembly (near `priority.invalid`; `findings: any[]` means no schema change) and keep human output coherent for a global (`itemId: null`) finding.
- `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` — shared probe/outcome (created by the parity-policy child).
- `tests/doctor-audit-fingerprint-skew.test.ts` (new) — unit matrix (skew / undeclared / ok / env-missing) using injected contracts.
- `tests/cli/doctor-audit-gaps.test.ts` — pattern reference for the CLI assertion.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `buildAuditFingerprintSkewFinding(outcome, ctx)` — pure: returns the warning finding for a `fail` outcome, `null` for `ok`/`skip`.
2. Probe once inside `wl doctor` (reusing the shared outcome helper) and push the finding when present.
3. Verify the human-output path: findings are grouped by `itemId` and printed as `
<itemId>`; a global finding must render sanely (e.g. under a `(global)` heading) or be surfaced via the existing advisory-notice style block, and must land in the "manual fixes required" grouping (no actionable `proposedFix`).
4. Tests: unit matrix + one CLI run asserting no skew finding on a schema-2 install.

## Definition of done

Unit + CLI tests green via the test skill; `wl doctor` and `wl doctor --json` both exercised; exit code unchanged in both cases.

## Verification

Parent AC4 satisfied by AC1–AC6; parent AC7 (full suite) is covered by the implementation gate.

## Dependencies

Depends on the parity-policy child (shared probe module `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts`).

## Goal

A full-suite run executed from the **main checkout** (e.g. the post-push/audit cache-evidence path) races sibling `implement.py finish` steps: `finish` fast-forwards the main checkout's local `dev` (git merge --ff-only) after pushing, swapping files on disk **while vitest is running**. A suite that starts at commit X but reads files half way through the run can load tests from commit X and source from commit Y (or vice versa), producing unrelated phantom failures. Discovered while verifying WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6.

## Evidence

WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 post-push verification (main checkout, commit 1abe9618): the canonical suite reported 4 failures in `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` and `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts`, all consistent with new-alphabet tests asserting against old-alphabet behaviour (local-preferred clamped to remote-ok; local-only not clamped). The main checkout reflog shows `merge refs/remotes/origin/dev: Fast-forward` to 2401d874 at exactly that moment (files touched by 2401d874 include packages/herdr/src/local-preference.ts, settings.ts, send-to-pi.sh and the failing tests, all with 22:47 mtimes). The exact same tree passed green in an isolated worktree (284 files / 4144 tests) minutes earlier.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Document the race (e.g. in docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md or the implement-skill reference) and/or mitigate it, e.g. run post-push cache-evidence suites against a pinned commit in an isolated worktree and graft the cache entry into the main checkout, instead of running in the live main checkout.
2. The race does not generate additional phantom test-failure items without manual triage.
3. Existing guidance (implement skill post-push verification step) is updated if behaviour changes.

## Problem statement

The per-turn local-preference route log (`<cwd>/.worklog/local-route.log`,
written by `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/` on
`after_provider_response`) is written by interactive panes but **not** by
headless `pi -p` sessions.

## Evidence (verification WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY, 2026-10-29)

- Headless run `01a187e9-2e34-72c3-b1b0-cf42d269c1a0` (`HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE=local-preferred`,
  `pi -p --model plan`, cwd = a project worktree): the preference header was
  sent (`routing_check … preference=local-preferred` in the proxy log), the
  client retried four 429 deferrals and completed locally, but **no**
  `local-route.log` line was produced in the session cwd.
- Interactive pane `01a18808-a7b1-75ff-b7d0-603be417e6cb` (same env, same
  worktree) wrote the expected line:
  `{"at":"2026-10-29T14:24:01.781Z","sessionId":"01a18808-…","preference":"local-preferred","route":"local","model":"plan"}`.

## Expected

A completed provider response in a headless session should produce the same
bounded route-log entry (the dispatcher's headless background dispatch,
`spawnBackgroundPi`, cannot be audited through the route log today).

## Investigation pointers

- Whether Pi emits `after_provider_response` on the `-p` stream path, and
  whether `event.headers` / `ctx.cwd` are populated there.
  - Verified on this build (plan review, 2026-10-30): the hook is emitted from
    the shared provider-response path (`handleProviderResponse` in
    `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, guarded only by
    `hasHandlers("after_provider_response")`), and the event payload carries
    only `{ type, status, headers }` — `cwd`, `sessionId` and `model` all come
    from the extension `ctx`. The headless gap is therefore most likely a
    `ctx` (cwd/session id) or lifecycle difference on the `-p` path rather
    than a missing emission; confirm before choosing a fix.
- If the hook is not emitted headless, either document the limitation in
  `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` / `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  (the reproduction section already carries a HEADLESS CAVEAT note) or capture
  the route from the same transport wrapper the recovery module installs.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` — hook registration (`before_provider_headers`, `after_provider_response`), `ctx.cwd` guard, bounded `appendRouteLogEntry`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/index.ts` — extension entry point wired through `packages/tui/extensions/package.json` → `pi.extensions`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts` — existing pure-module and hook tests (the deterministic coverage AC2 extends these).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.background.ts` — `spawnBackgroundPi` (line ~205), the headless dispatch path whose route evidence is currently missing.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — reproduction/verification section holding the existing "Headless caveat" note.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — extension contract documentation for the route log.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 A headless `pi -p` turn with `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` set either writes
  a route-log entry, or the limitation is documented as intended behaviour.
- AC2 A deterministic test covers the chosen behaviour.
- AC3 Existing route-log tests and the herdr/extension suites stay green.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (to the producer, non-blocking for implementation):** AC1
  offers two resolutions — write the entry headless, or document the
  limitation as intended. `## Expected` above implies the first is preferred
  (a headless dispatch cannot be audited without it), while AC1's second
  branch would be satisfied by the "Headless caveat" note already present in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`. Plan review left AC1 unchanged to avoid
  altering intent; implement should prefer the fix and fall back to
  documenting only if the `-p` path is proven not to carry `ctx` for
  extensions, recording the evidence in the work item. Raise if the
  documentation-only outcome is acceptable as the end state.

## Goal

**As** a producer or agent scanning the herdr worklist, **I want** each work item to show who holds it — an `Assignee` metadata row plus an `[assignee]` prefix on the item's title — **so that** I can tell a producer hold (`Map`) or an active agent claim apart from an unheld item at a glance, without opening the item or running `wl show`.

## Background

`assignee` is the claim/scheduling-hold field (see `AGENTS.md`: the producer sentinel is `wl update <id> --assignee Map`, released with `--assignee ""`; claim tiers write the agent name). It is already present end-to-end in the data layer — `wl show` / `wl list --json` return it and `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) parses it into `WorkItem.assignee` — but the herdr TUI never displays it. The `wl show` CLI already renders an `Assignee` row, so the CLI is out of scope.

Related work (not duplicates): WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR surfaces the *aggregate* "entire dispatch window held" banner (header count + warning banner), and WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 restored the per-item `Reviewed` metadata row + list icon — the closest precedent for this shape of change (shared `buildMetaRows` row, list/preview/detail parity, `noIcons` mode, README docs).

## Surfaces

- **Preview** — the selection-list metadata panel (`buildMetadataPanelLines` → `buildMetaRows`) and the hover tooltip.
- **Detail view** — the full item view (`formatDetailContent`: header title + shared metadata table).
- **List rows** — `formatItemLine` (selection list, browse feed and log-derived dispatch rows all render through it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `buildMetaRows` returns an `Assignee` row carrying the item's raw assignee value whenever `assignee` is a non-empty, non-whitespace string, positioned immediately after the `Effort` row so `pairMetaRows` compound pairing (Status+Stage, Priority+Type, Created+Updated, Audit+AuditedAt) can never absorb or reorder it; the row is omitted entirely when `assignee` is undefined, null, empty or whitespace-only.
- AC2: One shared helper (`formatTitleWithAssignee` in `worklist.format.ts`) returns `[<assignee>] <title>` for an assigned item and the byte-identical title for an unassigned one, and every title-rendering surface uses it: selection-list rows (`formatItemLine`), the preview metadata `Title` row, the detail-view header, and the hover-tooltip title line.
- AC3: Unassigned parity — for an item with no assignee every surface renders exactly as today: no `[] ` prefix, no leading space, no empty `Assignee` row, and the existing herdr suites pass unchanged.
- AC4: Rendering invariants hold — list rows still truncate within `maxCols` (display-width aware), the `[assignee] ` prefix inherits the title's priority colour, `noIcons` mode is unaffected, and `metadataPanelContentHeight` counts the extra row so the panel's `m`/`M` scroll clamp can still reach it.
- AC5: Visibility of a real hold — an item with `assignee: "Map"` renders `[Map]` before its title in the list row, the preview `Title` row and the detail header, and `Assignee  Map` in the preview panel and detail metadata table.
- AC6: `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the new `Assignee` row and the `[assignee]` title prefix in its metadata-panel, detail-view and hover-tooltip sections. The detail-view coverage may live inside the existing metadata-panel / design-decisions sections — a dedicated detail-view section is not required (producer decision 2026-10-30).
- AC7: Test coverage — each code AC (AC1–AC5) is covered by a test in the herdr vitest suite (`worklist.test.ts`, `worklist-tooltip.test.ts`, `worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts`), and the full gate is green at the implementation commit via `/skill:test`. (Reworded from "test-first ordering" by producer decision 2026-10-30: failing-test-before-implementation ordering is not verifiable from a squashed commit and is guidance, not an acceptance criterion.)

## Minimal implementation

1. **Test (red first).** Extend the existing herdr suites (`worklist.test.ts`, `worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts`, `worklist-child-coverage.test.ts`) with: assigned/unassigned `buildMetaRows` + `pairMetaRows` cases, `formatTitleWithAssignee` unit cases, assigned/unassigned `formatItemLine`, `formatDetailContent` header, `formatTooltipLines`, and `metadataPanelContentHeight` accounting.
2. **Helper.** Add `formatTitleWithAssignee(item)` (or `(title, assignee)`) to `worklist.format.ts` — the leaf formatting module — so `worklist.ts` (the not-yet-split monolith under the ≤1000-line shrink-only allowlist) does not grow logic.

# `wl update --status blocked` silently reverts to `open` and still reports success

Discovered while parking `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) on an assignee hold on 2026-10-29.

## Problem

On a specific item, `wl update <id> --status blocked` succeeds, prints `Status ⛔ Blocked`, returns `"status": "blocked"` in `--json`, and then the **stored** record is `open` — with an `updatedAt` 20–30 ms *after* the write that the command reported.

Reproduction (tce-main-street worklog, item `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`):

```
$ wl update MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4 --status blocked --json | jq -r .workItem.status
blocked
$ sleep 2; wl show MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4 --json | jq -r '.workItem.status + " " + .workItem.updatedAt'
open 2026-10-29T17:55:59.257Z      # the update's own record said 17:55:59.234Z
```

- Reproduced **4×**, including with `--if-status open`, and via the SQLite store directly (`workitems.status = 'open'`, `updatedAt` = the later timestamp).
- **Not** a sync artefact: `.worklog/last-sync-time` was `17:24:20Z`, well before the writes, and no other `wl` process touched the item (`downtime-*.log`, `local-route.log` checked).
- The revert is specific to **`status`**: `--assignee Map` and `--do-not-delegate true` writes on the same item persist.
- The **create** path persists blocked: sibling items `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO` and `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR` (created with `--status blocked` by the plan) stay blocked.

Distinguishing feature of the affected item: it has **only an inbound** dependency edge (`MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` depends on it) and no outbound edges; its blocking reason is recorded in prose.

## Impact

An explicit status write that silently does not stick is a data-integrity hazard: a caller that blocks an item to stop `wl next` / auto-dispatch from starting it gets `success: true` and a rendered `Blocked` state, but the item stays schedulable. Here it would have allowed a verification child to be started against a prerequisite that has not landed — the exact failure the parent item's Q3 decision is about.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic reproduction exists as a test: create an item, give it an inbound edge only, `wl update --status blocked`, assert the **persisted** status is `blocked` (this currently fails).
- [ ] Root cause named on this item: which write path produces the second record and why it wins (candidates: a post-update re-sort writing from a pre-change snapshot; a derived-status reconciliation that maps blocked-without-outbound-edges to open; a second store/export mirror).
- [ ] Fixed so an explicit `--status blocked` either persists or **fails loudly** with the reason — never `success: true` with a silently different stored value.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the matrix: blocked with no edges; blocked with inbound edges only; blocked with outbound non-terminal edges; blocked with outbound terminal edges; and `--if-status` CAS interaction.
- [ ] The test names are cited on this item as evidence.
- [ ] Full node/pytest suites green for the change.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — status handling, re-sort after update.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` (line ~61 sets `status: 'blocked'` when an edge is added — the semantics the update path should agree with).
- `src/status-stage-rules.ts`, `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` — status/stage compatibility.
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` (`reconcileDependentStatus`) — the second write that reverts the status.
- `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`reSort`) — ruled out: writes only `sortIndex`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — SQLite writer used by the store (`worklog.db`); no second mirror.

## Evidence trail

- Origin: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street), comment `MS-C0MVTUG5U90041PQ1` and its follow-up.
- Workaround applied there so the hold is machine-enforced: `--assignee Map` + `do-not-delegate` tag on the affected child.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 (re-run): re-planned an item still at `intake_complete` although its decomposition and root-cause analysis were recorded on 2026-10-29. Verified the root cause against the current tree — `db.update` still calls `hooks.reconcileDependentStatus(id)` after a status/stage change (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`, `updateWorkItem`), that reconciliation still maps `blocked`-with-no-active-blockers to `open` (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`), and `db.update` still returns the pre-reconcile snapshot; `src/commands/update.ts:565` still performs the redundant post-update self-reconcile. Confirmed all cited Key Files exist, except the to-be-created `tests/regression-explicit-blocked-status.test.ts`. Tightened this item's Key Files to real paths (the `src/storage*/` / "worklog.db writer" bullets did not exist). Re-ran the six automated review stages and the AC coverage review (100% coverage by the four children); advanced the stage to `plan_complete`. No children were added, rewritten, or closed.

# Reproduce: `wl update --status blocked` silently reverts to `open`

Parent: WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82 (AC1 — deterministic reproduction). Test-first:
this task must land (and be proven red) before the fix task.

## Why this fails today

`db.update` writes the requested `blocked` status and then calls
`hooks.reconcileDependentStatus(id)` (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:312-322`).
That reconciliation rewrites `blocked` -> `open` whenever the item has **no
active outbound blockers** (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts:244-281`).
The update then returns the *pre-reconcile* snapshot, so `--json` reports
`status: "blocked"` while the store holds `open` with a later `updatedAt`.

The distinguishing feature of the affected item (inbound edge only, no
outbound edges) is exactly the condition that triggers the unblock.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic reproduction exists as a test: create an item, give it an inbound edge only, run `wl update <id> --status blocked`, and assert the **persisted** status is `blocked` (this currently fails).
- [ ] The same test asserts the JSON-reported `workItem.status` equals the persisted status (stored/reported agreement).
- [ ] The test fails against the current tree (reproduces the defect) and is named so it can be cited as evidence on the parent.
- [ ] No production code is changed in this task.

- Add `tests/regression-explicit-blocked-status.test.ts` following the harness in `tests/regression-auto-unblock.test.ts` / `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`; extend the existing file instead if its harness fits.
- Seed the affected item, add an inbound edge (`db.addDependencyEdge(other, item)`), invoke the update, re-read via `db.get`/`wl show --json`, and compare stored vs reported status.
- Record the failing output on this work item as proof the test reproduces the defect.

**Key Files:**
