# Fix: explicit `--status` writes must not be reconciled away

Parent: WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82 (AC2, AC3 — root cause named, blocked persists).
Depends on the reproduction task.

## Root cause (code-verified)

- `db.update()` calls `hooks.reconcileDependentStatus(id)` after any
  status/stage change (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:312-322`).
- `reconcileDependentStatus` rewrites a `blocked` item to `open` when
  `hasActiveBlockers()` is false (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts:244-281`)
  — i.e. any item with no outbound active dependency edge, including one the
  caller just explicitly blocked.
- `updateIfMatches` (CAS path) calls the same `update()` and therefore shares
  the defect (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:186-220`).
- `db.update` returns the pre-reconcile snapshot, so the CLI prints `blocked`
  while the store holds `open` with a later `updatedAt`
  (`src/commands/update.ts` JSON output path).
- `src/commands/update.ts:565` performs a second, redundant
  `db.reconcileDependentStatus(normalizedId)` after the update.
- Ruled out: the post-update `reSort` only writes `sortIndex`
  (`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts:446-457`), and the repro was
  confirmed against SQLite directly (no second store mirror).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl update <id> --status blocked` persists `blocked` for items with no edges, with inbound-only edges, and (unchanged) items with active outbound blockers.
- [ ] Fixed so an explicit `--status blocked` either persists or **fails loudly** with the reason — never `success: true` with a silently different stored value.
- [ ] An explicitly requested status is not overwritten by the self-reconcile in the `wl update` path; dependency-derived reconciliation is unchanged: `wl dep add` still blocks, `wl dep rm` still unblocks when no active blockers remain, and completing a blocker still unblocks its dependents.
- [ ] `db.update` and the CLI `--json` payload report the persisted post-reconcile record, not a pre-reconcile snapshot.
- [ ] Root cause named on this item: which write path produces the second record and why it wins — the derived-status reconciliation in `db.update` maps blocked-without-outbound-edges to open; the post-update re-sort and second store/export mirror candidates are ruled out.
- [ ] The reproduction test from WL-0MVTVYNY4001EBRX passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread an explicit-status signal from `src/commands/update.ts` into `db.update` / `db.updateIfMatches` (e.g. an option such as `reconcileSelf: false`) so an explicitly supplied `--status`/`--stage` is never self-reconciled.
- Keep `reconcileDependentsForTarget(id)` for dependents (blocker completion must still unblock them) and keep `dep add`/`dep rm` self-reconcile semantics.
- Re-read the persisted item after reconciliation and return it so callers observe final state.
- Remove or guard the now-redundant self-reconcile call in `src/commands/update.ts` (line ~565).

**Key Files:**
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
- `src/commands/update.ts`
- `src/commands/dep.ts`
- `tests/regression-auto-unblock.test.ts`

## Goal

Give the dispatcher a trustworthy, fail-closed **scope** signal (leaf vs parent)
for an audit candidate, from `wl show <id> --children --json`.

## Context

Parent: WL-0MSORQ8Y4004YT63, AC1. The audit tier selects root items only
(`--root-only`, WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC), so a candidate can be either a root leaf or
a root with children (an epic). The children count is the only input that
distinguishes a single-session audit (1 slot) from a parent audit that fans out
(parent + up to 2 children at `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New dep `getAuditCandidateScope(itemId, cwd)` on `DowntimeWorkerDeps` and the
  dispatch-contract dep type, implemented in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` with
  `wl show <id> --children --json`, `DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS` and
  `withTransientRetry` (same CLI discipline as the other wl-backed deps).
- Returns `{ ok: true, scope: 'leaf' }` only when a parsed `children` array is
  present and empty; a non-empty array → `{ ok: true, scope: 'parent' }`.
- Fail-closed: CLI error, timeout, parse failure, missing/non-array `children`, or
  a non-root candidate → `{ ok: false }`, and **every** caller treats `{ ok: false }`
  as `'parent'` (all-slots-style gate, no relaxed dispatch).
- Pure helper `classifyAuditScope(result)` in `downtime-worker.gates.ts` maps the
  dep result to `'leaf' | 'parent'` with the fail-closed default, exhaustively unit
  tested (C1 suite).
- Constant `DOWNTIME_LEAF_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 1` added to
  `downtime-worker.constants.ts` with a doc comment tying it to the leaf case.
- Parent AC1 traceability: "Audit-tier selection (`deps.getNextAuditCandidate` or `dispatchDowntimeWork`) fetches the candidate's children (`wl show <id> --children --json`; fail-closed → treat as parent, all-slots gate)." — satisfied by the `getAuditCandidateScope` dep, its fail-closed `{ ok: false }` → parent mapping and the classifier unit tests.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the dep interface docs + fixture default (C1) and the `index.ts` implementation.
- Add `classifyAuditScope` (pure) and the constant.
- Scope lookup is called only by the slices that need it (C3/C4) — this slice adds
  no dispatch-path behaviour.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts`

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts`

- Blocks: C3, C4.

data.description:
## Goal

Let a **leaf** audit candidate dispatch when only 1 trusted slot is free, while a
**parent** audit candidate keeps today's 2-slot minimum — on every selection path.

## Context

Parent: WL-0MSORQ8Y4004YT63, AC2/AC3. `auditEligible` is currently a tick-level
boolean (`freeSlots >= DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`) threaded into three paths:
the legacy tier chain (`dispatchDowntimeWork`), the Herdr list-head filter
(`dispatchFromHerdrList`, normal + critical-first audit scan), and the
coordination leader. Eligibility must become **per item** because it now depends on
the candidate's scope, not only on the slot count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `freeSlots >= DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`, behaviour is unchanged and
  **no scope lookup is performed** (zero extra `wl` calls in the normal case).
- In the band `DOWNTIME_LEAF_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS <= freeSlots < DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`
  (i.e. exactly 1 free slot), an audit candidate is scope-classified: a classified
  leaf is dispatched; a parent, or any `{ ok: false }` lookup, is skipped exactly as
  today (reason/token `audit-tier-budget-skipped`).
- The per-item minimum is applied identically on the legacy tier chain, the Herdr
  head filter (including the critical-first audit scan) and produces the same
  decision for the same candidate on all paths.
- Parent/unknown candidates remain byte-for-byte equivalent to today: the existing
  audit-tier, critical-first, gates and dispatch suites pass unmodified.
- `DOWNTIME_PANE_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` eligibility for non-audit tiers is untouched.

data.description:
## Goal

Make the **tick admission** leaf-aware: with only 1 of 3 slots free (idle for the
full threshold), the worker dispatches the leaf audit and nothing else.

## Context

Parent: WL-0MSORQ8Y4004YT63, AC2/AC4/AC6. Today the tick never reaches the
dispatch filters in that band: `pollAndEvaluate` sets `ready` only when
`ctx.perSlotTracker.thresholdMetCount(cfg.thresholdMs) >= cfg.requiredFreeSlots`
(`downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts:487-540`, default `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots`
= 2 of 3 — the item description's "default 0" is stale). Relaxing only the tier
gate (C3) therefore changes nothing in production. This slice relaxes the tick
requirement **for a classified leaf audit only**, pinned to that item, so no other
tier can consume the spare slot under the relaxed policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In per-slot mode, when `thresholdMetCount >= DOWNTIME_LEAF_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`
  (1) but `< cfg.requiredFreeSlots`, the tick peeks the audit candidate (existing
  `getNextAuditCandidate`, honouring the active-audit single-flight and freshness
  checks) and admits **only** if the candidate classifies as a leaf.
- The relaxed admission is pinned: the dispatched item for that tick is that audit
  candidate; implement/plan/intake and critical tiers remain ineligible because
  `panesEligible` still uses `cfg.requiredFreeSlots` (unchanged).
- Fail-closed: no candidate, `{ ok: false }` scope lookup, a parent candidate,
  `slots: []`, `slots_stale: true`, `capacity_hint: saturated`, contention or the
  prefill gate all restore today's behaviour exactly (no relaxation).
- Decision log records a non-blocking observation token `leaf-audit-admission`
  carrying `freeSlots`, `thresholdMetCount`, `requiredFreeSlots`, item id and scope;
  a relaxed tick that finds only a parent still emits `audit-tier-budget-skipped`.
- The per-slot idle tracker (WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG) supplies the same-slot identity:
  the same free slot must be continuously free for the full threshold (AC4), and a
  slot that starts processing resets only its own timer.
- Existing orchestrator/tick suites pass unmodified for `freeSlots >= requiredFreeSlots`.
- Parent AC2 traceability: "**Leaf candidate** (0 children): dispatch when at least 1 slot is free (`available_slots >= 1`) for the full idle threshold." — satisfied by the leaf-aware tick admission plus the per-item minimum, with the full idle threshold enforced by the per-slot tracker.
- Parent AC4 traceability: "Same-slot stability: the "same N slots free for the full threshold" guarantee requires per-slot identity — this item is BLOCKED BY LP-0MSORPUMX002LLIA (proxy exposes `slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]` in `GET /llama/local/status`). Until it lands, leaf dispatch keeps the all-slots gate (no behavior change)." — the enabler has landed (llm-manager/proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md) and same-slot stability is preserved through the existing per-slot idle tracker, so leaf dispatch no longer needs the all-slots gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `leafAuditAdmission` value to the tick context (null by default) computed in
  `pollAndEvaluate` when the leaf band is detected.
- Thread it into `performDispatch`/`dispatchDowntimeWork` so only the pinned audit
  candidate can use the relaxed budget.
- Add the decision-log token next to `audit-tier-budget-skipped`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on: C3.
- Blocks: C5, C6.

## Goal

Ship the **optional** race-accepting variant as an opt-in setting that is OFF by
default, preserving the fail-closed default policy (parent AC5).

## Context

Parent: WL-0MSORQ8Y4004YT63, AC5/AC6. Without per-slot identity a leaf audit cannot
wait for "the same slot free for the full threshold"; the race-accepting variant
dispatches on `available_slots >= 1` immediately, accepting that an interactive
request may take the slot and the audit's first call falls back to remote. Per-slot
identity **has** landed (LP-0MSORPUMX002LLIA — see
`llm-manager/proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`), so this is a documented
opt-in escape hatch, never the default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New setting `downtimeLeafAuditImmediate` (boolean, default `false`) added to the
  settings type/defaults/clamp path and read live per tick like the other downtime
  settings; absent or malformed → `false`.
- OFF (default): behaviour identical to C4 — full idle threshold required, then the
  leaf allowance applies.
- ON: a classified leaf audit dispatches on 1 trusted free unowned slot without
  waiting the full idle threshold; still fail-closed on `slots: []`,
  `slots_stale: true`, `capacity_hint: saturated`, live contention, the prefill
  gate and owned slots.
- The decision log records the toggle state on the `leaf-audit-admission` token, and
  tests assert both states plus the fail-closed matrix under ON.
- The setting is documented as opt-in with the race trade-off (docs slice C7).
- Parent AC5 traceability: "Optional (documented, not required): the race-accepting variant — dispatch on `available_slots >= 1` without per-slot identity, accepting that an interactive request may grab the slot and the audit's first call falls back to remote. Default OFF; fail-closed philosophy preserved." — the setting ships default OFF, documented as opt-in, with the fail-closed matrix asserted under ON.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the setting + clamp/validation alongside the other downtime knobs.
- In the leaf-admission computation, treat the toggle as a threshold bypass (still

# Refactor guard: worklist split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the
repo enforces these for `worklist.ts` today. The `downtime-worker` series
already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-30, `dev`, `worklist.ts` = 7,899 lines):

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and
   `downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` must stay **byte-identical and green** —
   duplicating the 28k-line scanner is not acceptable.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in
   `isSplitFamilyFile`, `splitFamilyModules`, `findBarrelValueImports`,
   `findSplitFamilyCycles` and `findDispatchInFlightDeclarations`; add a
   `--target worklist` branch to the `--write-baseline` CLI.
2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import … from './worklist.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes, dedupe, sort →
   `worklist.split-baseline.json` with provenance fields (expect 66 symbols).
3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,
   single-owner, cycle/barrel, size+allowlist, baseline provenance), each as a
   separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   sources parsed by the same helpers) and assert each gate reports a failure.
5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child
   (`WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N`) can empty it in one line.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — minimal parametrisation (defaults preserved)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — must stay unchanged and green

## Constraints

- Additive only: adding a test file and a parametrisation hook does not violate
  parent AC3 ("no test file is modified").
- No production `worklist*.ts` edits in this child — it lands first, alone.
- No new runtime dependencies (`typescript` is already used by `scan.ts`).

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- Precedent: `WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E` (downtime-worker split guard) — same shape,
  same AC numbering, already green on `dev`.

## Target outcome

A deterministic, read-only structural gate for the `src/github.ts` decomposition lands **before** any production code moves, so the six extraction children cannot regrow the god class or quietly change the public surface. Mirrors the shipped `src/sync.ts` split guard (`tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` + `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` + `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json`, WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and the `packages/shared/src/database/` guard (WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A guard suite exists at `tests/github/github-split-guard.test.ts` (with scanner `tests/github/github-split-guard-scan.ts` and frozen baseline `tests/github/github.split-baseline.json`) and passes against the **unmodified** pre-split tree.
- The baseline records the frozen public surface of `src/github.ts`: 58 plan-time symbols, classified as 52 value exports and 6 type-only exports (`GithubConfig`, `GithubIssueRecord`, `GithubIssueComment`, `IssueHierarchy`, `AssignGithubIssueResult`, `LabelEvent`), sorted and deduplicated, with reproducible provenance.
- The guard fails if any baseline symbol stops being exported from `src/github.ts`, or if a new public export is added beyond the baseline.
- The guard fails if any file in the github family (the `src/github.ts` barrel and every `src/github/**/*.ts`) exceeds 1,000 lines, using a **shrink-only** allowlist whose only entry is `src/github.ts` at its current 1,755-line ceiling; the guard fails if an allowlisted file is no longer oversized (allowlist may only shrink).
- The guard fails if any module under `src/github/` imports the `src/github.ts` barrel (runtime or type-only), and fails on any static or runtime import cycle in the github family.
- The guard fails if a github-family production module lacks a top-level JSDoc header naming its concern.
- Every gate is proven to fail on deliberately broken input (self-tests using `indexFromSources`-style synthetic modules), so a silently no-op gate is caught.
- No production file under `src/` is modified by this item; the existing suite still passes unchanged.
- All existing tests pass without modification to their import paths or assertions (move-only, behaviour-preserving). [inherited from parent AC]
- No file (original or extracted module) exceeds 1,000 lines. [inherited from parent AC]
- Public exports from the original module path remain importable unchanged (barrel re-export where consumers exist). [inherited from parent AC]
- No new circular imports; module responsibilities documented. [inherited from parent AC]
## Minimal implementation

1. Add the scanner: reuse the exported parsers from `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` (`parseModuleSource`, `resolveImportTarget`, `findStronglyConnectedComponents`, `collectExportKinds`, `namesOfKind`, `hasLeadingJsDoc`, `isTypeOnlyImport`, `MAX_MODULE_LINES`) via import — do not copy the 942-line scanner.
2. Add small additive optional parameters to the sync scanner where a family/barrel is currently hardcoded (`splitFamilyModules`, `buildImportGraph`, `findBarrelImports` gain an optional family/barrel argument defaulting to the current sync values). This is backwards compatible: `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` must stay green and unmodified.
3. If parameterisation proves invasive, fall back to implementing the family filter, graph build and barrel-import scan locally in `tests/github/github-split-guard-scan.ts` (~150 lines) using only the pure parsers — record the choice in the work item.
4. Generate the baseline with a `--write-baseline` CLI entry point and commit it as a frozen contract (regenerate deliberately, never to make a red gate green).
5. Record the guard → parent-AC mapping in the suite's header JSDoc.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/github/github-split-guard.test.ts`
- `tests/github/github-split-guard-scan.ts`
- `tests/github/github.split-baseline.json`
- `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts`
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`
- `src/github.ts`

## Constraints

- Test-first: this item lands before any extraction child; no `src/` file changes.
- Additive only: no change to existing test assertions or import paths (`tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` must pass unmodified).
- No new dependencies: parse with the TypeScript syntax API only, no program/type-checker.
- Guard runs in one vitest file, well under the ~2 s gate budget.

## Risky assumptions and mitigation

- **Assumption:** `src/github.ts` and a new `src/github/` directory can coexist under NodeNext resolution (`./github.js` resolves to `src/github.ts`, submodules import `./github/transport.js`). **Mitigation:** verified by the repo's shipped `src/sync.ts` + `src/sync/` split, which has the same shape.
- **Assumption:** the 58-symbol surface is complete. **Mitigation:** the baseline is generated from the live barrel and reviewed once; the guard then freezes it.
- **Risk:** additive scanner parameterisation breaks the sync guard. **Mitigation:** defaults preserve current behaviour; the sync guard suite is the regression check, and the documented fallback avoids touching it at all.

## Parent acceptance criteria covered

- AC1 (no file over 1,000 lines): enforced by the shrink-only size gate with a `src/github.ts` ceiling of 1,755 that can only shrink.
- AC2 (public exports from the original module path stay importable): enforced by the frozen 58-symbol baseline, value-resolution and type-declaration gates.
- AC3 (existing tests pass without modification): this item adds no behaviour change and must leave the whole suite green.
- AC4 (no new circular imports; responsibilities documented): enforced by the barrel-import ban, cycle gates and the JSDoc-header gate.
- AC5 (related documentation updated; full suite passes): the guard documents the contract it enforces in its own header JSDoc.

# Remove the heartbeat skill (superseded by the downtime dispatcher)

## Problem statement

The `heartbeat` skill (`/skill:heartbeat`) predates the herdr downtime dispatcher and duplicates — while contradicting — it. It is not in use: no invocation appears anywhere in the Pi session archive, and nothing in `wl`, the herdr plugin, cron, systemd or the test suite calls it. Keeping it costs two drifted copies of the same script that must both be maintained, plus a second, off-contract work-item ranking path.

## Evidence gathered (2026-10-30)

**No usage:**

- `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: zero occurrences of `/skill:heartbeat` as a user prompt (`"text":"/skill:heartbeat"` → 0 files); the ~1,000 hits are the skill-catalogue description embedded in every system prompt.
- No tool-result output of a real run (`"Flagged … for producer review"`, `"No items in completed/in_review queue"`) anywhere in the archive — those strings appear only inside the skill's own source/SKILL.md text.
- No crontab entry, no systemd timer, no herdr plugin hook, no caller in `packages/herdr/src` (the only "heartbeat" hits there are the unrelated *sync* heartbeat), no reference from any other skill.

**Superseded by the downtime dispatcher** (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`):

| | `heartbeat` skill | Downtime dispatcher |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | manual `/skill:heartbeat`, one action per call | continuous, leader-elected idle dispatch |
| Audit invocation | headless `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>`, 600 s timeout, invisible | visible herdr pane, with pane monitor, stall resume and attempt budget |
| Audit threshold | review queue ≥ 10 (hard-coded) | review-queue gate `count >= browseItemCount` (live setting) + depth-aware audit batching |
| Candidate ranking | `wl next` — a **second ranking path** | "dispatcher == Herdr list head"; a second ranking is explicitly disallowed |
| `needsProducerReview` | set as a "look at this next" nudge on a sparse queue | a **dispatch hold**, set only on attempt-budget exhaustion |

**Duplicate drift:** `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` (resolved at runtime) and `skill/heartbeat/` (imported by the tests) are separate git-tracked copies that have diverged in their audit dispatch (`pi -p` vs `audit_runner.py`); the parity guard in `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` exists only to stop further divergence. Removal eliminates the drift by construction.

**Deliberate coverage loss:** automated audit dispatch without herdr. The dispatcher lives in the herdr plugin and requires idle local-LLM capacity; a herdr-less mode would need a new implementation against the dispatcher's contract. Accepted — there is no herdr-less deployment today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/heartbeat/` and `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` are removed from the repository, so `/skill:heartbeat` no longer resolves in Pi and no duplicate copy remains.
2. `tests/skill/heartbeat/` (unit and integration suites) is removed; no test imports or references the heartbeat module.
3. The `README.md` feature blurb and the docs table row advertising the heartbeat skill are removed.
4. Stale prose is corrected: `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` no longer lists heartbeat as a `wl` consumer (inventory table and both summary rows), and `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` no longer refers to "heartbeat tooling" as a queue consumer.
5. The superseded work items recorded as deleted with the dispatcher named as the replacement: heartbeat audit notifications (WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI) and the `.pi` copy-drift item (WL-0MVVM0SLV0053QP8). *(Both were soft-deleted at filing time; this AC needs no implementation work — verify only that nothing still references them.)*
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (CHANGELOG.md is release-managed and excluded).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/heartbeat/` — delete (SKILL.md, `scripts/heartbeat.py`, `__init__.py`).
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` — delete (runtime copy).
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py`, `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat_integration.py` — delete alongside the skill.
- `README.md` — remove the feature blurb (~line 11) and the docs table row (~line 140).
- `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — drop heartbeat from the `wl`-consumer inventory and per-invocation rows.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — reword the "heartbeat/release tooling" reference (~line 74).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — remove the heartbeat entry from the known skill-behaviour-drift note (~line 735) if it becomes stale.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher is the sole replacement for background audit dispatch; no herdr-less automation exists to preserve.
- **Assumption:** the "ready for producer review prior to a new release" report has no unique consumer (the ship/release gate and worklist header cover it); if that changes, it belongs in the worklist header, not a standalone skill.
- **Risk — muscle memory:** a user typing `/skill:heartbeat` will now get "skill not found" rather than a silent no-op. Accepted; the failure is loud and harmless.
- **Risk — stale references:** prose in `docs/dev/` and the README mentions the skill in several places; AC4 covers the substantive ones and a repo-wide grep for `heartbeat` (excluding the unrelated sync heartbeat and `CHANGELOG.md`) should come back clean.
- **Scope creep guard:** do not port heartbeat's sparse-queue nudge into the dispatcher — `wl reviewed <id> true` plus the TUI icon already cover manual producer flagging.

## Related work

- `Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)` — the original item, now superseded.
- `Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane (WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7)` — documents the headless-visibility gap that led here.
- `Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (WL-0MSACL482002RNYH)` — the toast plumbing the (withdrawn) notification proposal would have reused.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the replacement mechanism.

## Problem

`tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts` runs its fixture `git()` helper with `env: { ...process.env, PATH: realGitPath() }`. That inherits any repository-override variable the caller exported — notably `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, which `implement.py finish` sets to a temporary index while it validates the would-be-commit tree (`implement-gate-*.index`).

With `GIT_INDEX_FILE` inherited, the fixture's `git add`/`git commit` write into the gate's temporary index, whose object references belong to the implementation worktree. The gate then (correctly) refuses the run as unattributable:

```
gate evidence invalid: the temporary index changed while the suite ran (tested tree c98d11b..., index now c7f9016...). A test staged into the inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE instead of its own repository's index.
```

and the fixture itself then fails with `error: invalid object 100644 ... for '.worklog/config.yaml'` / `error: Error building trees`, so three sync-concurrency tests fail for an infrastructure reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The fixture's git helper invokes git with a hermetic environment that drops the repository-override variables (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, config overrides), so a leaked value can never redirect the fixture's git commands.
2. The suite still passes when run with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing at an unrelated temporary index (asserted by a test that sets it and then exercises the same fixture path).
3. No behaviour change for a normal run (no `GIT_INDEX_FILE` in the environment).

## Evidence

Discovered while finishing WL-0MVV1EZVB007M1LR (leaf-aware audit dispatch C3): `implement.py finish` fell back to full scope (custom `suiteCommands`) and the gate reported the index mutation above.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts`

# Profile in-process CLI harness per-call cost

**Parent:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost
**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want one repeatable profile of a single `runInProcess()`
invocation that attributes its wall-clock cost to named phases, so that the
reuse work in WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY (children 2–4) targets the phase that
actually dominates instead of guessing.

## Context

Every `runInProcess()` call currently constructs a fresh `Command`, registers
~29 built-in commands, calls `createPluginContext(program)` (which calls
`getDefaultDataPath()` and builds output helpers), applies the
`--worklog-dir` override, parses argv, and — for any command that performs
data access — opens a SQLite database (schema + migrations) which is closed in
the harness `finally` block. Seed measurements were ~72 ms for `--help` (no DB
work) and ~196–257 ms for `list --json` / `create` / `status`, but the split
between commander registration, config load, DB open/migrate and the command
action has never been measured per phase. This child is the measurement stage
(parent AC 1) and the evidence base for the parent's re-scope decision
(parent AC 3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action)
  for at least four scenarios: `--help`, `list --json`, `create`, `status`.
- Each scenario reports its buckets in milliseconds and as a share of the
  call, with the nested phases inside those buckets recorded: argv
  split/normalisation, `Command` construction, built-in command registration,
  `createPluginContext`, worklog-dir override application, database open
  (including schema creation/migrations), database close, command action, and
  harness bookkeeping (stream/console patching plus throttler drain).
- Phase attribution reconciles to **≥ 90 %** of the total measured per-call
  wall time for each scenario; the residual is reported explicitly as
  "unattributed harness overhead" rather than silently dropped.
- Each scenario reports the **median of ≥ 3 runs** on the same host, with the
  host load average and the exact commands recorded alongside the numbers.
- The pre-change baseline for this item is published as a new
  "In-process CLI harness cost" section in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`
  containing the attribution table, host/load context, run count, and the path
  to the machine-readable JSON artefact.
- The published attribution explicitly answers the parent's decision gate: it
  names the dominant phase for the ~196–257 ms path and classifies the cost as
  **harness-side** (test-harness overhead) or **production startup** (`src/`
  behaviour: DB schema/migrations, plugin scan, config load), with that
  phase's share of the total stated in milliseconds and percent.
- The profiler is bounded and safe to run repeatedly: a full run completes in
  under 60 s on the reference host, uses temp worklog directories only (never
  the repository `.worklog/`), and cleans up after itself.
- The profiler is invocable by a documented, single command (an `npm run`
  script or a documented `npx tsx bench/...` invocation) — it is not a vitest
  test, so it is run directly and never through an ad-hoc vitest invocation.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts`, modelled on the existing
   `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` / `bench/startup-budget.ts` precedent (JSON
   artefact + human table, `--runs`, `--json`, `--update-baseline` style
   flags).
2. Obtain phase marks without changing default harness behaviour: add an
   opt-in instrumentation hook to `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` (e.g. a
   `WL_INPROC_PROFILE=1` env switch that appends `{phase, ms}` marks to an
   exported collector, default off), or a thin profiling wrapper that re-times
   the same phases from outside. Default-path behaviour and timing must be
   unchanged when the switch is off.
3. Instrument DB open/close via the existing `ctx.utils.getDatabase` wrapper
   the harness already installs, and command action via the existing
   `preAction`/`postAction` hooks.
4. Emit a JSON artefact plus a Markdown table and paste the table into the new
   `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` section.
5. Note in the section that the numbers are same-host medians and that
   absolute values are load-sensitive (the parent's stated measurement risk).

## Key Files

- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts` — new profiler entry point.
- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — phase instrumentation hook (default off).
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — `execAsync` call path under measurement.
- `bench/startup-budget.ts`, `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` — precedent for
  artefacts, flags and host-load reporting.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — new baseline section.
- `package.json` — `benchmark:`/`bench:` script entry.

## Dependencies

- None. This child unblocks the parent's re-scope decision and children 2–3.

## Deliverables

- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts` (bounded, temp-dir-only, JSON artefact).
- Opt-in, default-off phase instrumentation in the in-process harness.
- New "In-process CLI harness cost" baseline section in
  `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` with the attribution table and the
  harness-side vs production-startup verdict.

## Notes / constraints

- Do not run the test suite to produce these numbers; the profiler is a bench
  script. Any suite run needed later goes through the test skill
  (`/skill:test`), never an ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test` call.
- Observed while planning (out of scope here, do not fix in this child): the
  mock-bin `PATH` setup at the top of `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` references
  `fileURLToPath` without importing it, so that block silently throws and the
  mock-bin prefix is never applied in-process. Record it as an observation in
  the work item; do not bundle the fix into this child.

# Reuse-safety and harness-contract tests (test-first)

**Parent:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want tests that characterise the in-process harness
contract *and* prove that any cross-call reuse actually happens, so that
child 3 can reduce per-call cost without silently making tests
order-dependent, and so the improvement itself is test-first (red before the
implementation lands).

## Context

Parent risk (fidelity): caching a `Command`/plugin context, a parsed config,
or a DB connection across calls can leak commander option state or the global
`--worklog-dir` override (`setWorklogDirOverride` / `_worklogDirOverride` in
`src/worklog-paths.ts`) between tests, producing order-dependent passes. The
existing `tests/cli/inproc-harness.test.ts` covers only one create→update
round trip. This child is the test-first stage: it lands before the
implementation child and must fail (on the "reuse actually happens" contract)
until that child lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Consecutive in-process invocations with **alternating `--worklog-dir`**
  values (two temp worklogs, calls interleaved A→B→A) each report only their
  own worklog's items — no leakage of the override or of the resolved data
  path between calls.
- **Global-option state does not leak**: after a `--json` call, the next
  non-`--json` call produces human output (and vice versa); the same holds for
  `--verbose` and `-F/--format`; a `-w/--watch` option present in one call
  does not survive into the next.
- **Read/write coherence**: within one process, `create` → `list --json` →
  `update` → `show --json` against a single worklog observes each preceding
  mutation (a shared or cached DB handle must not serve stale data).
- **Restoration contract**: after every call, `process.argv`, `process.exitCode`,
  `process.stdout.write`, `process.stderr.write`, `console.log/error/warn/info`
  and `process.exit` are restored to their pre-call identities, and the
  harness's returned `exitCode` reflects a command that set `process.exitCode`
  or called `process.exit`.
- **Reuse contract (must be red before child 3):** an exported instrumentation
  counter in the harness (e.g. `getInprocHarnessStats()` reporting
  `commandsConstructed`, `pluginContextsCreated`, `databasesOpened`) shows the
  pre-change cost of **one construction + one DB open per call**, and the test
  asserts the post-change expectation (≤ 1 per reused call for the stateless
  read path) — the red evidence is recorded on this work item before child 3
  starts.
- **Order independence**: running the same mixed sequence of read/write calls
  in reverse order yields byte-identical stdout per call — catching
  order-dependent leakage.
- All new tests run in-process only (no subprocess spawns), complete in under
  5 s, and do not change any existing test's assertions or counts.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `tests/cli/inproc-harness-reuse.test.ts` with the fidelity/order cases
   above; reuse `createTempDir`/`cleanupTempDir` from `tests/test-utils.ts`
   and the config/init helpers in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`.
2. Add the minimal, always-on `getInprocHarnessStats()` counter to
   `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` (counter increments only — no behaviour change)
   so both the contract test and the budget guard in child 4 can read it.
3. Mark the reuse-contract assertion as the red-first case: run it before
   child 3 lands, capture the failure, and record the output on this item.
4. Keep `tests/cli/inproc-harness.test.ts` as-is; extend it only if a case
   genuinely belongs to that file's single-round-trip scope.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/inproc-harness-reuse.test.ts` — new test file.
- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — counters (`getInprocHarnessStats()`).
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — `execAsync`/temp-dir/config helpers.
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `--worklog-dir` override semantics under test.
- `tests/cli/inproc-harness.test.ts` — existing harness test (reference).
- `tests/test-utils.ts` — `createTempDir` / `cleanupTempDir`.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: child 1 (WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY profile) — the attribution decides
  which reuse surfaces (command/context vs config vs DB) need characterising.
- Blocks: child 3 (implementation) and child 4 (budget guard).

## Deliverables

- New fidelity/order/restoration test file, green against the current harness.
- Harness instrumentation counters (behaviour-neutral).
- Recorded red evidence for the reuse-contract assertion on this work item.

# Budget guard and consolidated docs for harness cost

**Parent:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the measured in-process harness cost locked in by an
automated guard plus a documented before/after record, so a future change
cannot quietly reintroduce the ~200 ms per-call cost and so the suite-runtime
claim is auditable.

## Context

Parent AC 4 requires the canonical suite to stay green with unchanged test
counts and improved median wall clock versus this item's own pre-change
baseline; parent AC 5 requires the measured improvement (or, in the re-scope
branch, the documented finding) to be encoded in an automated test or
benchmark assertion; parent AC 6 requires all related documentation to be
updated. The repository already has the exact precedent for this:
`bench/startup-import-budget.json` + `bench/startup-budget.ts` +
`tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`, a checked-in ratchet with
host-load-tolerant pass/fail (CPU-time gate, wall normalised by a bare-node
control, clamped host-load factor). This child reuses that pattern rather than
inventing one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A checked-in budget artefact (e.g. `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json`)
  records, per profiled scenario (`--help`, `list --json`, `create`,
  `status`), the measured per-call cost produced by child 1/child 3, with the
  measurement host, load average, run count and date recorded in the artefact.
- At least one automated test or benchmark assertion encodes the measured
  improvement (or, where the outcome is a recorded finding, a documented
  baseline that a regression test can compare against): the budget artefact
  plus its guard test.
- The guard test `tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts` reads that artefact
  and fails when the current per-call cost exceeds it plus a documented
  headroom; the gate is host-load tolerant along the
  `bench/startup-import-budget.json` lines (CPU-time-based comparison, or wall
  normalised by a same-run bare-node control, with the factor clamped) so a
  contended host does not flake it. The headroom and its rationale are
  documented in the test's header comment, and the guard adds < 5 s to the
  suite — it re-uses recorded numbers or measures a small bounded number of
  in-process invocations.
- In the re-scope branch (cost is production startup, no harness change
  landed), the guard still exists but asserts the documented baseline:
  it fails if the artefact is missing, unparseable, or its schema/keys drift —
  so a regression test compares against a documented baseline even when no
  improvement was achieved.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock on
  a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item,
  measured through the test skill (`/skill:test`, full scope, `--type full`)
  as the median of at least two runs with the host load average quoted.
- The before/after record quotes each run's host load average, the test and
  file counts (unchanged), the delta against the child 1 baseline, and the
  caveat that wall clock on a shared host is noisy.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Documentation specifics: the "In-process CLI harness cost" section in
  `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` is finalised with problem, root cause,
  change, before/after table, the standing rule that harness per-call cost is
  budget-guarded, and the guard's run command; comments at the reuse/cache
  sites explain keys and invalidation; and any docs-site entry, `README.md` or
  `CLI.md` is updated only where behaviour or contributor guidance actually
  changed (explicitly stated when nothing needed changing).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, evidenced by the
  test skill at full scope, with no ad-hoc test invocations.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` (schema version, per-scenario
   baselines, headroom, `$comment` pointing at the regeneration command).
2. Add `tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts` modelled on
   `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`, reading both the artefact and
   child 2's `getInprocHarnessStats()` counters.
3. Add the regeneration entry point (extend `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts`
   with `--update-budget`, mirroring `npm run benchmark:wl-startup --
   --update-budget`).
4. Run the full suite twice through the test skill, capture the summaries and
   host load, and record medians plus deltas.
5. Finalise the `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` section and sweep the
   code/README/CLI.md comments.

## Key Files

- `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` — new checked-in ratchet.
- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts` — `--update-budget` mode.
- `tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts` — new guard test.
- `bench/startup-import-budget.json`, `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`
  — precedent for schema, headroom and host-load tolerance.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — finalised harness-cost section.
- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — counters and cache-comment sites.
- `README.md`, `CLI.md` — review only; update only if guidance changed.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: child 3 (implementation or recorded re-scope finding).

## Deliverables

- Checked-in budget artefact with host/load provenance.
- Host-load-tolerant guard test with documented headroom.
- Before/after canonical-suite measurement (test-skill evidence, medians,
  host load, unchanged test counts).
- Finalised `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` section and updated code/docs
  comments.

# Reduce in-process harness per-call overhead (or record re-scope)

**Parent:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the per-invocation cost of the in-process CLI harness
reduced where that cost is test-harness overhead, so the ~1200 in-process
invocations in the suite stop costing ~240 s of aggregate wall clock — without
changing what any test asserts. Where the cost is genuinely production CLI
startup instead, I want that recorded and re-scoped rather than papered over
inside the test harness.

## Context

Child 1 publishes the per-phase attribution; child 2 lands the fidelity tests
that make cross-call reuse safe to attempt. This child acts on the
attribution. The parent's explicit candidates are: reusing the
`Command`/plugin context across calls for stateless reads, avoiding repeated
YAML config parses (`loadConfig`/`loadConfigRelaxed` in `src/config.ts` read
and `yaml.load` the config files on every `getDatabase()`), and sharing the DB
open across calls within a test file. The parent's AC 3 requires that if the
dominant cost is production startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan), the
finding is recorded and the change re-scoped into `src/` instead of being
worked around in the harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Decision gate recorded first:** the work item carries a comment quoting
  child 1's attribution numbers and stating whether the dominant cost is
  harness-side or production startup, naming the dominant phase and its share
  of the ~196–257 ms per-call cost. No code is written before this decision is
  recorded.
- **Harness-side branch (parent AC 2):** where the cost is test-harness
  overhead (not production behaviour being asserted), reduce it without
  changing what each test asserts — using the candidates of reusing the
  command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads, avoiding repeated
  YAML config parses, and sharing the DB open across calls within a test
  file, only where child 1's attribution justifies it. Median per-call cost
  for `list --json` and `status` drops by **≥ 30 %** versus the child 1
  baseline, measured on the same host as the median of ≥ 5 runs with load
  average quoted.
- **Production-startup branch (parent AC 3):** if the cost is production CLI
  startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan), record the findings and
  re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a production decision,
  not a test-only change — no in-harness workaround is added, and a
  `discovered-from:WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY` work item is created for the `src/`
  change (scoped to schema/migration bootstrap, plugin scan, or config parse),
  and this child closes with that recorded finding plus the documented
  baseline — satisfying parent AC 3 instead of parent AC 2.
- **Zero behavioural change:** every existing test keeps its assertions and
  the suite test count is unchanged; child 2's fidelity, order-independence
  and restoration tests are green, including alternating `--worklog-dir` and
  mixed read/write sequences.
- **Reuse-contract assertion flips green:** child 2's `getInprocHarnessStats()`
  assertion for the reused read path (≤ 1 command construction / DB open per
  call) passes, and stdout for each call is byte-identical to the
  pre-change output for the same command line.
- **Cache correctness is explicit:** every cross-call cache or shared handle is
  keyed and invalidated on the state that can change it (resolved worklog
  directory, config file mtime/content, DB schema version), the invalidation
  keys are stated in a code comment at the cache site, and a test exercises at
  least one invalidation path (config edited between calls, worklog dir
  changed between calls).
- **Scope containment:** changes stay inside `tests/` (harness and helpers)
  plus test-facing docs/comments; no behavioural change to `src/` production
  code paths. Anything that would require a `src/` change is re-scoped per the
  production-startup branch.
- **Suite evidence:** the affected and full suites are run through the test
  skill (`/skill:test`), not ad-hoc test commands, and the results are quoted
  on the item with the host load average.

## Minimal implementation

1. Post the decision-gate comment from child 1's artefact; choose the branch.
2. Harness-side branch (typical, if child 1 confirms the DB/config path
   dominates): enable a per-process cache inside `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`
   keyed by `getWorklogDirOverride()`/resolved worklog dir, covering the
   parsed config and the opened DB handle; reuse the `Command` + plugin
   context only for commands declared stateless reads; reset all caches in the
   harness when the key changes.
3. Keep `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` unchanged as a call site —
   any caching must be transparent to it.
4. Re-run the child 1 profiler to produce the after numbers; record both
   before/after medians and the delta on the item.
5. Production-startup branch: record the finding, create the `src/`-scoped
   follow-up item, and close without code changes to the harness.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — command/context/config/DB reuse and cache keys.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — `execAsync` call site (must stay unchanged).
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `getDatabase` (calls `loadConfigRelaxed` per call) and
  `createPluginContext`; read-only unless the branch is production-startup.
- `src/config.ts` — `loadConfig` / `loadConfigRelaxed` YAML parse cost.
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `setWorklogDirOverride` /
  `applyWorklogDirOverrideFromArgv` global override (cache key + invalidation).
- `src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` open/schema/migration bootstrap.
- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts` — profiler used for before/after numbers.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: child 1 (profile/attribution) and child 2 (reuse-safety tests).
- Blocks: child 4 (budget guard and consolidated docs).

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate comment with attribution numbers and chosen branch.
- Harness reuse/caching implementation with documented cache keys and
  invalidation, or (re-scope branch) the recorded finding plus a new
  `src/`-scoped work item.
- Before/after profiler medians and the measured per-call delta on the item.
- Test-skill evidence for the affected and full suites.

# Intake Brief: hydrator must not demote `in-progress` claims held by pane-less driven sessions

Created from `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK` (llm store) per producer decision Q1 = **B**: the defect record lives here now; the reporting item was deleted after this item was created and synced.

## Problem statement

`decideDemotion()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts:497`) treats *"no pane title in this workspace contains the item ID"* as *"nobody is working this item"* and releases the claim (`in-progress/* → open/intake_complete`, or `blocked` / `completed` on the other branches) on every 30 s cycle. A **driven child session** — `implement.py drive` → `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>"` — is headless by design (`WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7`) and therefore can never produce a matching pane, so every claim it makes is reverted within one cycle while it is still editing. The same single-signal rule also releases items whose herdr pane title no longer contains the ID.

## Users

- **Driven/headless implement sessions** (`implement.py drive` / `phase` / `start`) — as a driven session, my `in_progress` claim must survive while my process is alive, so `StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` does not fail mid-work and no second session is handed the same item.
- **Producer / operator** — as a producer, `in_progress` must mean "someone is actually working this", *and* abandoned claims must still self-heal without manual intervention.
- **Dispatching agents** (`wl next`, the downtime worker) — as a dispatcher, I must never receive an item a live session is editing (the duplicate-dispatch failure `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` exists to prevent).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Live claim holder suppresses demotion.** An item that is `in-progress` with **no** matching pane but whose `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is currently **held** (non-blocking `flock` fails with `EWOULDBLOCK`) is left untouched by the cycle. Covered by a unit test that takes a real flock in the test process.
2. **Dead holders are still released (no regression to stuck claims).** An item with a lock file whose `flock` is free **and** whose recorded `pid` is not alive is demoted exactly as today (`open`/`intake_complete`), within one cycle — covered by a unit test using a stale fixture lock.
3. **Existing decision branches are unchanged.** Pane match ⇒ untouched; no lock file ⇒ demoted; active outbound dep blocker ⇒ `blocked`; stage `in_review` ⇒ `completed`; a held claim never overrides the `blocked`/`in_review` branches — all covered by tests.
4. **Fail-open on ambiguity.** An unreadable lock directory, a malformed/corrupt lock file, or an unexpected `fs`/`flock` error **suppresses demotion** and logs a named reason (mirroring the existing `wl`/`herdr` fail-open), rather than releasing the claim — covered by a test per error class.
5. **Pid-reuse guard.** The `pid` fallback is only trusted when the lock's `started_at` is not earlier than the recorded process start time; otherwise the probe reports *held* (fail-open) and names the reason in the log, so a recycled pid can never be read as a live claim — covered by a test with a fabricated stale `started_at`.
6. **Cost stays bounded.** The lock directory is read **once per cycle**, with no additional `wl`/`herdr` spawns per item and no wall-clock TTL/heartbeat; a test asserts the spawn and directory-read counts for a multi-item cycle.
7. **Release clears the scheduling hold (Q3 = A).** When the hydrator releases a claim it also clears `assignee` (`wl update … --assignee ""`) and records the previous holder in the release audit comment (e.g. `released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: implement`). A test asserts the `wl update` argument vector and the comment body; live verification: after a release, `wl show <id>` reports an empty `assignee` and the release comment names the previous holder.
8. **Diagnosable log lines.** Every suppression and every release names the deciding signal, e.g. `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder pid <pid> session <sid>` and `[hydrator] released <id>: … (no pane, claim holder dead)` — existing hydrator log-format tests extended.
9. **Docs updated.** `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` (Design step 3 + Safety list) and the `hydrator.ts` module header describe the second signal, its fail-open rules, the pid-reuse guard, the `assignee`-clearing behaviour, and the explicit non-goal (no TTL / no heartbeat).
10. **Producer directive reconciled.** The docs restate and keep the producer's rule — "It should be simple. Look for a pane in this workspace with the work item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy." (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`, quoted at `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md:58`) — as the **primary** signal, with the claim holder added as a second, mechanically verifiable signal for pane-less sessions.
11. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
12. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm run build` + `npm test` in the repository root).

## Constraints

- **Keep the pane rule primary.** Pane-title matching was chosen after the producer rejected tab-label matching as unreliable (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`); add to it, do not replace it.
- **No new protocol, no TTL.** The claim signal is the existing per-child lock produced by `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` (installed from SorraAgents). It is **kernel-authoritative while held** and its file **persists after release**, so existence and `started_at` age are never liveness evidence — only `flock` heldness (with the guarded `pid` fallback) is.
  - Measured 2026-10-31 on the llm store: 40 `child-*.lock` files, **all** recording pids that were no longer alive. An existence check would suppress demotion forever.
- **Read the lock contract defensively.** `{agent, pid, session_id, started_at, token}` is a diagnostic sidecar; unknown or extra fields must not break the probe, and `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy means a holder chain (driver → `parent`/`start` subprocess → driven child) may present the same token.
- **Budget.** A cycle already races a 5 s per-step budget inside a 20 s run watchdog (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS` / `HYDRATOR_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ`); the probe must be local `fs` I/O only, resolved from the worklog root already available via `getWorklogDir()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`).
- **Fail-open asymmetry is deliberate.** Ambiguity ⇒ no demotion; affirmative death ⇒ release.
- **Scope.** Do not redesign dispatch, the worklist selection marker, the drive orchestrator, or `implement.py`. Adjacent opportunities (hydrator log rotation, orphaned-lock cleanup) are separate items.

## Evidence (captured from the reporting store before its log rotated)

`.worklog/logs/hydrator.log` in `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`, window 2026-10-31T04:10–04:37Z — ten releases, three items, all `in-progress/intake_complete → open/intake_complete (no matching pane)`:

| Time (UTC) | Item | Releases | State after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 04:10:59, 04:11:29, 04:28:30 | `LP-0MVT1NVAJ007KUGO` | 3 | later `blocked/intake_complete` |
| 04:14:59, 04:15:29, 04:31:00, 04:31:30, 04:32:00, 04:36:31 | `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` | 6 | `open/intake_complete`, `assignee=Map` (stale hold — AC7) |
| 04:29:30 | `LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12` | 1 | completed in_review by its own session |

Earlier evidence (2026-10-30T20:49–20:52Z, `LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO`, three releases interleaved with the live session's writes) had already rotated out: `hydrator.log` keeps only the live ~200-line window with no archive. Also unverified and therefore recorded as *reported, not reproduced*: a release of `LP-0MVSAM2AV0077UAE` attributed to a herdr pane whose id changed.

## Desired change

A cycle decides "busy" from two independent signals and demotes only when both are negative:

1. **Pane signal (unchanged, primary)** — a pane in the current workspace whose title contains the item ID ⇒ busy.
2. **Claim-holder signal (new)** — a **live** claim holder for the item: `child-<id>.lock` currently flocked, or the guarded pid fallback ⇒ busy.

## Fix specification

1. **Extend the injected deps** with `hasLiveClaimHolder(itemIds): Promise<Map<string, boolean>>` (batch over the cycle's candidate list) alongside the existing `HydratorDeps` seams, so orchestration stays unit-testable with no real filesystem.
2. **Decision input.** Add `held` to the `decideDemotion()` context and return `null` when `ctx.hasActivePane || ctx.held`; keep the `blocked` / `in_review` ordering untouched.
3. **Probe.** Resolve the worklog root once per cycle, enumerate `locks/child-*.lock` once, then per candidate: non-blocking `flock` (acquire succeeds ⇒ release immediately and fall back to guarded `pid` liveness; `EWOULDBLOCK` ⇒ held; missing file ⇒ not held; any other error ⇒ held + named log reason).
4. **Release path.** Pass `--assignee ""` on the demotion `wl update` and append the previous holder to the audit comment (Q3 = A).
5. **Tests** in `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — one per AC 1–8, using a temp worklog root with real `flock` fixtures.
6. **Docs** — `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` and the module header (ACs 9–10).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `decideDemotion()` (line 497), the orchestration cycle (`runHydrationOnce`), `HydratorDeps` (line ~246), `createProductionHydratorDeps().applyDemotion` (line 1030): add the claim-holder signal, the heldness probe, and `--assignee ""`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new decision, probe and orchestration cases (1,348 lines today).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `getWorklogDir()` / `buildWlArgs()` already resolve the store root the probe needs.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — Design step 3 + Safety list + Files section.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` — lock contract being read (read-only; `agent`/`pid`/`session_id`/`started_at`/`token`, `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy).
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the holder population (`_new_child_lock` / `_set_child_lock`, ~lines 696–760); read-only.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI` (completed) — *Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane*: introduced this demotion rule and `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` (completed) — the producer's pane-title directive and the selection-list marker.
- `WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US` (completed) — *Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items*: AC3 defines the `open`/`intake_complete` release target.
- `WL-0MTTSWE0G008M1VA` (deleted, folded into `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`) — the "no pane ⇒ stale regardless of age" claim-age rule this item qualifies.
- `WL-0MTWU4Y82001B3UH` (completed) — demotion must leave an audit-trail comment (extended by AC7).
- `WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ`, `WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO`, `WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX` (completed) — per-step budgets, stdio isolation and bounded ticks constraining the probe.
- `WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI` (completed) — hydrator docs/pane-title rationale, the doc to update.
- `WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7` (completed) — *Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless `pi -p` vs herdr pane*: why driven sessions have no pane.
- `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` — *actively worked ⇒ `in_progress`* invariant (SorraAgents store), the contract this violates.
- `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` — per-child lock rationale (`drive` duplicate-session RCA).
- `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK` (llm store) — the defect report this item was created from (deleted after this item was created and synced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — pid reuse.** A stale lock whose pid now belongs to an unrelated process would suppress demotion indefinitely. Mitigation: `flock` is authoritative; the pid fallback is gated on `started_at` (AC5) and logged.
- **Risk — cross-repo coupling.** The hydrator would depend on a lock format owned by the globally installed skills. Mitigation: defensively parse (unknown ⇒ fail-open), document the contract in `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, and keep the probe behind an injected seam so the source can change without touching orchestration.
- **Risk — re-introducing stuck claims.** Any suppression that outlives the holder re-creates `WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI`'s original defect. Mitigation: no TTL, kernel liveness only, AC2 test.
- **Risk — cost creep per tick.** A per-item filesystem probe over a large in-progress list. Mitigation: one directory read per cycle, map lookup per item (AC6).
- **Assumption.** The `implement.py` lock is held for the whole driven-session lifetime (`phase_start` through session exit), so it is a faithful "session is alive" proxy — verified in `implement.py` (`_set_child_lock` / `_release_child_lock`, released in the phase cleanup and by the kernel on crash).
- **Assumption.** A pane-less session may still be *pane-visible* if a wrapper later spawns one; the change is a strict superset of the current signal, so no existing behaviour is narrowed.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Log rotation, orphaned-lock cleanup, drive-orchestrator changes: separate items, not scope here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 "Should the fix be raised as a work item in this store, with the llm report item deleted once created and synced?"** — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-31): B — "b, once created and synced delete this item"**: create the implementation item here, sync, then delete `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK`. Source: producer reply on `LP-0MVVG8BAT00238JK`; evidence: this item's creation, the sync in this store, and the deletion reason on the reporting item.
- **Q2 "Which pane-less claim signal should the hydrator honour?"** — **Answer (producer): A** — the existing per-child lock `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, probed for *heldness* via non-blocking `flock` with a guarded pid-liveness fallback. Research: `work_item_lock.py` (kernel releases the flock on exit/SIGKILL; metadata is diagnostic only); 40/40 existing lock files on the llm store recorded dead pids, so heldness — never existence — is the signal.
- **Q3 "When the hydrator releases a claim, should it also clear `assignee`?"** — **Answer (producer): A** — clear it and record the previous holder in the release audit comment; a released item must not stay parked on a scheduling hold (live example: `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` was `open/intake_complete` with `assignee=Map` after its 04:36:31Z release, because `applyDemotion` passes only `--status`/`--stage`).
