# Cross-repo dependencies: discover sibling project stores, resolve foreign blockers, request a clone when absent

## Goal (headline)

`wl` can **record, resolve and honour dependency edges whose target lives in
another project's store**, discovered automatically from sibling folders, so a
consumer item can be genuinely blocked by an upstream item in a different
repository instead of by a prose note that no tool enforces. When the foreign
project is not present locally, `wl` asks the producer for its git URL and
clones it.

**Created at the producer's direction (2026-10-31)** while unblocking
LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X (llm repo): that item is blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB
(SorraAgents) across stores, `wl dep add` cannot express the edge
(`Work item not found`), and `blocked` does not persist without an edge — so
the consumer's guard child reported `open` and looked startable, which would
have landed a red test. The producer chose to fix this in the tool rather than
by a placeholder item.

## Users and user stories

- **Implementing agent** — "As an agent working on a consumer item, I want the
  upstream item in another repository to block me mechanically, so I cannot
  start work whose precondition does not exist yet."
- **Producer** — "As the producer, I want the tool to discover the projects on
  this machine by itself and, when one is missing, tell me exactly what to
  clone instead of failing with `Work item not found`."
- **Framework maintainer** — "As the owner of the agent skills, I want one
  resolution rule in `wl` core so the skills stop re-implementing a
  prefix→sibling scan (there are already two copies)."

## Current behaviour (measured 2026-10-31)

| Observation | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Cross-store edges cannot be recorded | `wl dep add <local-id> <foreign-id>` → `Work item not found: <foreign-id>` (`src/commands/dep.ts` validates both endpoints against the local DB only) |
| `blocked` cannot stand in for the edge | `wl` reconciles `blocked`→`open` from the edge graph; an item with no edge cannot hold `blocked` (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` `reconcileBlockedStatus`) |
| Blocker semantics live in one predicate | `isDependencyActive()` — `status` in `completed`/`deleted` or `stage` in `in_review`/`done` is inactive; everything else blocks |
| The prefix→sibling scan already exists twice outside `wl` core | `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/work-item-title.ts` (WL-0MVGB23MM004X501) and the skills layer `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`) |
| Store discovery must not be fooled by worktrees | every implement/audit worktree checks out `.worklog/config.yaml`, so `/worktree/.worklog/` exists but holds no data — `isGenuineWorklogStore()` (`src/worklog-paths.ts`) is the existing discriminator (`initialized` or `worklog.db`) |
| Framework classifies cross-prefix edges as coordination notes only | SorraAgents `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`wl_dep_blockers`, `coordination_blockers`, SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T) |

## Required behaviour (design constraints)

**D1 — Discovery.** Scan a *projects root* (default: the parent directory of the
current checkout; overridable via config, e.g. `projectsRoot: <path>`) for
**immediate subdirectories** that hold a **genuine** local store
(`isGenuineWorklogStore`, i.e. `.worklog/initialized` or `.worklog/worklog.db` —
presence of `.worklog/` alone is NOT sufficient, because worktrees carry a
tracked `config.yaml`). Build a `prefix → <project>/.worklog` map from each
store's `config.yaml` `prefix`. Deterministic (sorted), memoised per process,
no repository-wide walk. A duplicate prefix declared by several projects is
**reported as ambiguous**, never silently picked. Non-git folders, hidden
folders and managed worktrees are excluded.

**D2 — Recording foreign edges.** `wl dep add` / `dep rm` / `dep list` accept an
id whose prefix belongs to a discovered sibling store. The foreign endpoint is
resolved **read-only** (open the sibling DB read-only; never write, never sync,
never take a mutation lock on it) purely to validate existence and to read its
title/status/stage. The edge is stored in the **local** store with the foreign
id as target, and same-project behaviour (including the automatic `blocked`
status flip) is unchanged.

**D3 — Gating on foreign targets.** Every place that evaluates dependency
blockers (`isDependencyActive` consumers: `wl next`, `wl worklist`, `wl list`,
`doctor` dependency check, `dep list`) resolves a foreign target's
`status`/`stage` from its own store using the **same** terminal semantics as
today. Fail-safe: if the foreign store is missing, unreadable, or the target
cannot be resolved, the dependent **stays blocked** and the blocker is reported
with `unresolved: true` + a reason in JSON — it never silently unblocks.

**D4 — Missing project: ask, then clone.** When a dependency id's prefix has no
discovered store, do not report a bare `Work item not found`. Emit an actionable,
machine-readable result (`success: false`, `error_code: "unknown_project"`,
`prefix`, `projects_root`, `remediation`) that asks the producer for the git URL,
plus the exact command to run:

```
wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url> [--path <projects-root>/<name>]
```

`wl project add` records the mapping in the project config, clones the
repository when the path does not exist (`git clone <url> <path>`), validates
that the cloned store's `prefix` matches, and is idempotent (re-running on an
existing correct clone is a no-op). It must **not** read stdin by default —
agents cannot answer prompts — an explicit `--interactive` may prompt for the
URL. A failed clone leaves no config mapping behind.

**D5 — Sync isolation is preserved.** The existing cross-project guards
(`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `prefix-filter.ts`) still refuse a sync that would
merge foreign-prefix items; a sibling store is never exported, imported, synced
or locked against its owner's own `wl` writes. Regression tests pin both.

**D6 — One implementation, consumers converge.** The scan lives once, in `wl`
core, exposed through a JSON surface (`wl project list --json`,
`wl dep list --json` foreign entries). The two existing copies (TUI title
resolver, skills `status_lifecycle.py`) become follow-ups that call it; the
framework change that makes the implement skill treat a **resolvable**
cross-repo edge as a real blocker (rather than a coordination note) is a
separate SorraAgents item — out of scope here, recorded in Related work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Discovery.** A test tree with several sibling projects (one with
  `tests` support, one without), a worktree-shaped stub `.worklog/` (only
  `config.yaml`), a non-git folder and two projects declaring the same prefix
  yields: only genuine stores discovered, deterministic sorted `prefix → path`
  output, duplicate prefix reported as ambiguous, and a config override of the
  projects root honoured.
- **AC2 — Foreign edge recorded, foreign store untouched.** `wl dep add` with a
  foreign id succeeds, the edge is listed by `dep list` with the foreign title
  and status, the local dependent is set to `blocked`, and the sibling DB's file
  (content hash and mtime) is unchanged. Same-project `dep add`/`rm`/`list`
  output is byte-identical to today (regression).
- **AC3 — Gating.** An item whose only active blocker is a foreign item is
  excluded from `wl next` and included with `--include-blocked`; the same item
  becomes selectable once the foreign item reaches `in_review`/`done`/
  `completed`/`deleted`; a removed sibling store leaves the item blocked with
  `unresolved: true` and a reason in JSON (never unblocked).
- **AC4 — Missing project remediation.** An unknown prefix produces
  `error_code: "unknown_project"` with the projects root and the exact
  `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url>` remediation; `wl project add` clones
  into the projects root, records the mapping, validates the prefix, and is
  idempotent; a prefix mismatch or clone failure exits non-zero without leaving
  a mapping behind; no stdin prompt without `--interactive`.
- **AC5 — Sync isolation.** Existing cross-project sync guard and prefix-filter
  tests still pass, plus a new test proving a foreign store is opened read-only
  (no write, no lock) while a foreign edge is recorded and evaluated.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `CLI.md` (`dep`, new `project` command),
  `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md` and `README.md` document cross-repo dependencies,
  the discovery rule, the fail-safe `unresolved` behaviour and the clone
  remediation; `wl dep --help` states that foreign ids are supported.
- **AC7 — Full suite green.** The ContextHub suite passes via the test skill
  with no duplicate collection and no cache-key collision, including the new
  cross-repo test module.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/dep.ts` — accept and validate foreign endpoints, JSON fields
- `src/commands/project.ts` — **new**: `wl project list|add` (discovery +
  clone remediation)
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `getDatabase`/`normalizeCliId` and any new resolver hook
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `isGenuineWorklogStore` (reused) + projects-root resolution
- `src/config.ts` — `projectsRoot` and prefix→path mapping
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — `isDependencyActive` /
  `getActiveDependencyBlockers` foreign-target resolution and fail-safe
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` — `buildEdgeCache` (foreign items
  cannot be in the local edge cache; the resolver must not assume they are)
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — blocked-candidate filtering
  and blocker surfacing for foreign blockers
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — dependency check reporting unresolved foreign edges
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts`, `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — isolation guards
  (expected unchanged; regression-pinned)
- `tests/cross-repo-dependencies.test.ts` — **new** primary test module
- `tests/database-dependencies-comments-extraction.test.ts`,
  `tests/doctor-dependency-check.test.ts` — regression
- `CLI.md`, `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md`, `README.md` — documentation

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: scanning cost / surprise I/O.** Mitigation: one readdir of the
  projects root plus two `existsSync` probes per candidate, memoised per process;
  a missing/unreadable projects root is a warning, never an error.
- **Risk: ambiguity.** Two projects claiming the same prefix cannot be resolved
  safely → report, do not guess (probe-by-lookup, as the TUI resolver does, is
  acceptable only when it disambiguates a single owner).
- **Risk: semantic change for existing consumers.** Today the *framework* treats
  cross-prefix edges as coordination notes and never blocks on them. If the
  resolver starts returning `unresolved`-blocked for such edges, a consumer that
  previously ignored them could stall. Mitigation: fail-safe is `blocked` only
  when a real foreign store is discovered; an undiscoverable prefix stays a
  non-blocking coordination note until `wl project add` resolves it — state this
  explicitly in the JSON (`foreign_dependency: "resolved" | "unresolved" |
  "unavailable"`).
- **Assumption (documented, producer confirmable):** projects are siblings under
  a common projects root (today `/home/rgardler/projects/<project>`), each with
  its own `.worklog/` and a distinct `prefix` in `config.yaml`.
- **Assumption:** `git clone` uses the operator's existing git credentials; the
  tool never prompts for credentials.
- **Risk: TUI/skills duplication drift.** Mitigation: D6 names the follow-ups;
  this item does not edit the TUI or the skills.

## Out of scope

- Making the SorraAgents implement skill gate on cross-repo edges (separate
  framework item; recorded in Related work).
- Cross-*machine* / remote-store dependencies (only local sibling clones).
- Auto-cloning without a producer-supplied URL.
- Merging or syncing foreign stores, or exposing their items in this project's
  list/search surfaces (only dependency resolution reads them).

## Related work

- **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X** (llm) — the consumer item that needs a *resolvable*
  cross-repo edge to its upstream SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB; it is parked awaiting
  that upstream fix and this capability.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** (SorraAgents) — the "cross-project edges are
  coordination notes, never blocking" assumption this work supersedes.
- **WL-0MVGB23MM004X501** — TUI footer prefix→sibling resolution (the first
  in-tree copy of the scan).
- **WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST** — cross-project sync guard (the isolation contract D5
  must keep).
- **WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF** — shared `wl next`/`wl worklist` browse feed (the
  single selection path that AC3 must extend, not fork).
## Plan (plan_complete, 2026-10-31)

### Feature breakdown — tracer-bullet vertical slices, test-first

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Cross-repo fixture harness and discovery spec (WL-0MVWEEK24000S3TW) | task | — | AC1 |
| F2 | Discovery module and `wl project list` (WL-0MVWEELAW005SDLU) | feature | F1 | AC1, D1, D6 |
| F3 | Foreign dependency edge and isolation spec (WL-0MVWEEMP2002N37W) | task | F2 | AC2, AC5 |
| F4 | Foreign dependency edge CRUD (WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC) | feature | F3 | AC2, D2 |
| F5 | Foreign blocker gating and fail-safe spec (WL-0MVWEEP4U003FR91) | task | F4 | AC3 |
| F6 | Resolve foreign blockers in gating paths (WL-0MVWEEQ8K0013DOY) | feature | F5 | AC3, D3 |
| F7 | Project add remediation and clone spec (WL-0MVWEER72000TT6G) | task | F6 | AC4 |
| F8 | Implement `wl project add` and remediation (WL-0MVWEES9J0035SG6) | feature | F7 | AC4, D4 |
| F9 | Cross-repo dependency documentation (WL-0MVWEETA9006LFED) | docs | F8 | AC6 |
| F10 | Sync isolation and full-suite verification (WL-0MVWEEU5Z004E4K1) | task | F9 | AC5, AC7 |

Each child is a vertical slice through code, tests, docs and observability
(JSON fields, `wl doctor` findings, debug logging). Test/verification children
(F1, F3, F5, F7, F10) are ordered **before** the implementation child that turns
them green, per the test-first rule.

### Phasing (between-phase guidance)

- **Phase 1 — discovery (F1→F2).** After F2 lands, re-read F3/F4 descriptions:
  the discovery API shape (`discoverProjects`) is now concrete, so F3's fixture
  usage and F4's resolver signature should be checked against it before starting.
- **Phase 2 — foreign edges (F3→F4).** After F4, re-read F5/F6: the
  `foreign_dependency` tri-state is now implemented, so F5's gating assertions
  must match the emitted field names exactly.
- **Phase 3 — gating (F5→F6).** After F6, re-read F7/F8: the `unknown_project`
  payload is shared between `dep` and `next`, so F7 must assert the same shape
  F6 emits for `unresolved`.
- **Phase 4 — remediation (F7→F8).** After F8, F9 documents only behaviour that
  is now test-covered; F10 then verifies isolation and the full suite.

### Sequencing note

The chain is declared strictly linear (F1→F2→…→F10) for a single implementer.
F7's only technical prerequisite is F2 (discovery), and F9's are F6+F8; the
extra edges are deliberate serialisation, not hard dependencies.

### Deliberately deferred (out of scope, per this item)

Per **D6** and "Out of scope", the two existing prefix→sibling scan copies are
**not** converted here and no follow-up items are created yet (this item's own
wording: "create as `discovered-from` once this lands"):

- TUI title resolver — `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/work-item-title.ts`
  (WL-0MVGB23MM004X501).
- Skills layer — `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`).
- SorraAgents implement-skill gating on resolvable cross-repo edges
  (SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T) — separate framework item.

### Reused existing implementations (no new duplication)

- `isGenuineWorklogStore()` — `src/worklog-paths.ts` (worktree-stub discriminator, D1).
- `isDependencyActive()` — `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`
  (terminal semantics reused, never forked, D3).
- `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` (`src/sync/repo-context.ts`) and
  `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` (`src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`) — isolation guards
  kept and regression-pinned (D5).
- `tests/test-utils.ts` temp-dir helpers; `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` CLI harness.
- Lazy command registry pattern — `src/command-registry.ts` (for `wl project`).

### Documented assumptions (producer confirmable)

1. **Projects are siblings under a common root** (today `/home/rgardler/projects/<project>`),
   each with its own `.worklog/` and a distinct `prefix`. Default `projectsRoot`
   is the parent directory of the current checkout's git root.
2. **Config storage for the mapping**: `projectsRoot` plus a `projects:` map
   (`<PREFIX>: { path, gitUrl }`) live in `.worklog/config.yaml`, matching the
   item's "records the mapping in the project config". No new config file.
3. **Git credentials** come from the operator's existing git configuration; the
   tool never prompts for credentials (item's stated assumption).
4. **`--interactive` is opt-in only**; every default path is non-interactive so
   agents (which cannot answer prompts) never hang.
5. **Unknown-prefix compatibility**: an undiscoverable prefix stays a
   non-blocking `foreign_dependency: "unavailable"` coordination note, so
   existing consumers that ignored cross-prefix edges do not stall (item risk
   mitigation, made explicit in the JSON).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking questions were needed: the item already carried a full design
(D1–D6), seven acceptance criteria and a predicted key-file list, so the
planning decisions below were resolvable from the item and the codebase. Each is
recorded as a **decision with evidence** rather than an invented answer.

- **Q (self-answered): Is the autoplan pre-check's `skip` decision authoritative?**
  Answer (plan agent): No. `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` returned
  `Extra Small` / `Low`, but the effort-and-risk run recorded O=M=P=0.00h, risk
  0/25 and `assumptions: ["Auto-generated by autoplan decision"]` with no WBS —
  a zeroed placeholder, i.e. *undeterminable*, which the skill maps to
  `do_plan = True`. Evidence: `wl show WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD --json` (7 ACs, D1–D6,
  ~15 key files, new CLI command, new test module). Full planning performed;
  recorded in a work-item comment (2026-10-31).
- **Q: Is planning required at all, or is the item already decomposed?**
  Answer (plan agent): Required. `wl list --parent WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD` was
  empty and `stage` was `intake_complete`. Evidence: `wl show --children --json`
  returned `children: []`.
- **Q: Does a duplicate already implement this?** Answer: No full duplicate.
  Partial overlap only, on discovery. Evidence: `wl search "cross-repo"` /
  `wl list "cross-project"` → **WL-0MLYTK4ZE1THY8ME** (completed epic,
  multi-project *discovery + proposal* flow) overlaps D1's scan but covers no
  dependency-edge, gating or clone behaviour; **WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST**
  (cross-project sync guard) is the isolation contract D5 must preserve;
  **WL-0MSALMGTH002YXN7** (foreign-item detection) is the inverse concern
  (keeping foreign items *out*). No child was closed as a duplicate; F2 reuses
  the discriminator already shipped by those items rather than re-implementing it.
- **Q: Where does the prefix→path mapping live?** Decision: `.worklog/config.yaml`
  (`projectsRoot`, `projects:` map) — the item's D1/D4 both say "project config";
  no new file invented. Recorded as assumption 2 (producer confirmable).
- **Q: Must `blocked` survive a vanished foreign store?** Decision: yes —
  `isDependencyActive(null) === false` today, so an unresolved foreign edge would
  silently unblock. F5 pins it and F6 fixes it (item D3 "never silently
  unblocks"). Evidence: `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`
  `isDependencyActive` / `hasActiveBlockers`.
- **Q: Do the two existing sibling-scan copies get refactored here?** Decision:
  no — deferred per D6 and "Out of scope"; recorded above with file paths and
  item ids so the follow-ups can be filed with `discovered-from` later.

# Claim-holder probe: heldness detection with fail-open tests (test-first)

Parent: WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY — *[bug] hydrator demotes in-progress claims of pane-less driven sessions (no matching pane)*.

Phase 1 of the fix (test-first foundation). Nothing consumes the probe yet — the
cycle wiring is the sibling child *Busy = pane OR live claim holder*.

## Goal (user story)

As the hydrator, I need one local, side-effect-free way to answer "is this item's
`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` currently held by a live claim holder?" so the
cycle can treat a pane-less driven session as busy — *Live claim holder suppresses
demotion* — instead of releasing its claim while it is still editing.

## Context the implementer must not re-derive

- The claim signal is the existing per-child lock written by
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` (installed from SorraAgents):
  `{agent, pid, session_id, started_at, token}`.
- It is **kernel-authoritative while held**: the advisory `flock` is dropped on
  exit / `SIGKILL` / crash.
- The lock **file persists after release**, so existence and `started_at` age are
  never liveness evidence. Measured 2026-10-31 on the llm store: 40 `child-*.lock`
  files, **all** recording pids that were no longer alive — an existence check
  would suppress demotion forever and re-create WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI's stuck-claim
  defect.
- `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` re-entrancy means a holder chain (driver →
  `parent`/`start` subprocess → driven child) may present one token against one
  file.

## What to build

- New module `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — pure local `fs`/`flock` probing
  (no `wl`, no `herdr`, no network), exporting something shaped like
  `probeClaimHolders(itemIds, opts): Promise<Map<string, ClaimHolderVerdict>>`
  where the verdict carries `held: boolean`, a named `reason`, and the diagnostic
  metadata (`pid`, `sessionId`, `agent`, `startedAt`) when readable.
- Batch by design: **one** directory read of `<worklog>/locks/` per call, then a
  per-candidate heldness probe.
- Every seam injectable (fs reader, lock prober, pid-liveness/process-start probe,
  clock) so orchestration stays unit-testable with no real filesystem — the same
  style as the existing `HydratorDeps`.
- **Mechanism decision (spike, measured and documented).** Two candidates were
  verified working on the dev host on 2026-10-31:
  1. `flock(1)` spawn, e.g. `flock -n [<path>|fd] true` — rc 0 free, rc 1 held;
     portable; **warns**: plain `flock -n <path> true` *creates* a missing file
     (this host's `flock` 2.41.3 has no `--no-create`), so an fd-redirect form
     (`sh -c 'flock -n -E 75 9 9<"$1"' sh <path>`) must be used to avoid creating
     or truncating lock files.
  2. One `/proc/locks` snapshot per cycle (lines look like
     `6: FLOCK ADVISORY WRITE 2976141 00:2f:2632970 0 EOF`) plus one `stat` per
     candidate to map device+inode — zero spawns, Linux-only, needs a fallback
     when `/proc/locks` is unavailable.
  Record the chosen mechanism, the rationale and the **measured** per-candidate
  cost in the module header and `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`. Non-negotiables for
  whichever mechanism wins: no lock file may be created, truncated or rewritten by
  a probe; a probe must never block (no waiting for the lock); 50 candidates must
  stay far inside the 5 s per-step budget (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- TDD order: write the contract tests first (they fail), then implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Live claim holder suppresses demotion (unit half):** a lock file currently `flock`ed by another process is reported `held` — the test takes a REAL flock from a spawned holder process and asserts the probe sees it.
- [ ] **Dead holders are still released (no regression to stuck claims):** a stale fixture lock whose `flock` is free **and** whose recorded `pid` is not alive is reported not held, so demotion remains possible.
- [ ] Missing file: a candidate with no `child-<id>.lock` is reported not held, with zero spawns and no file created.
- [ ] **Fail-open on ambiguity:** an unreadable/unenumerable `locks/` directory, a malformed or corrupt lock file, and an unexpected `fs`/`flock` error each report `held` with a distinct named reason (mirroring the existing `wl`/`herdr` fail-open style), never a release.
- [ ] **Pid-reuse guard:** the `pid` fallback is trusted only when the lock's `started_at` is not earlier than the recorded process start time; otherwise the verdict is `held` with a named reason (test with a fabricated stale `started_at`), so a recycled pid can never be read as a live claim.
- [ ] **Cost stays bounded:** a 50-candidate batch performs exactly one lock-directory read and no per-item `wl`/`herdr` spawn — asserted through the injected reader/spawner counters.
- [ ] No side effects: after probing a mixed batch, the `locks/` directory contents (names, sizes, bytes) are unchanged (test).
- [ ] Defensive parsing: unknown/extra lock-file fields and a token-bearing (re-entrant) holder never break the probe (tests); the probe never writes the file.
- [ ] Mechanism + measured cost recorded in the `claim-lock.ts` module header and `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`.
- [ ] Changed-scope test gate green via `/skill:test` and `npm run build` clean.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — new probe module (mechanism + verdicts).
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.test.ts` — new contract tests: temp worklog root, real `flock` holder process, stale fixtures, error classes.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — module-header cross-reference only (wiring is the sibling child).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `getWorklogDir()` resolves the store root the probe needs.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — mechanism note.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/work_item_lock.py` — read-only lock-contract source.

## Out of scope

Cycle wiring / `decideDemotion`, the release path (`--assignee ""` + audit
comment), log-line changes, docs rewrite — all sibling children.

# Busy = pane OR live claim holder (decision + cycle wiring)

Parent: WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY — *[bug] hydrator demotes in-progress claims of pane-less driven sessions (no matching pane)*.

Phase 2: the end-to-end behaviour slice that fixes the reported defect. Depends on
*Claim-holder probe: heldness detection with fail-open tests*.

## Goal (user story)

As a driven / headless implement session (`implement.py drive`), my `in_progress`
claim must survive the hydration cycle while my child lock is held, so
`StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` never fails mid-work and no second session is
handed the same item (the duplicate-dispatch failure SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 exists to
prevent).

## Context the implementer must not re-derive

- The pane signal stays **primary and unchanged** (producer directive, WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ):
  a pane in the current workspace whose title contains the item ID ⇒ busy.
- The claim holder is a **second, mechanically verifiable** signal for pane-less
  sessions; this change is a strict superset of today's behaviour — no existing
  signal is narrowed.
- **Branch precedence (decided during planning, AC3 of the parent):** `held` is
  evaluated *after* the `in_review` and `blocked` branches, so a held claim never
  overrides them:
  `not in-progress → null` · `hasActivePane → null` · `stage in_review → completed`
  · `blocked → blocked` · `held → null` · `else → open/intake_complete`.
  Only the release-to-`open` branch is suppressed by a live holder (that is the
  reported defect); the audit-tier `in_review → completed` and the dependency
  `blocked` transitions keep their current behaviour.

## What to build

- `HydratorDeps` gains an **optional** batch seam
  `hasLiveClaimHolder?(itemIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, ClaimHolderVerdict>>`
  (optional so existing test fakes keep compiling). Production wiring in
  `createProductionHydratorDeps()` delegates to `probeClaimHolders` from
  `claim-lock.ts`, resolving the worklog root ONCE per cycle (`getWorklogDir()`,
  already imported there).
- `decideDemotion(item, ctx)` gains `ctx.held: boolean` and returns `null` for
  `ctx.hasActivePane || ctx.held`, **keeping the documented ordering above**.
- `runHydrationOnce`: compute the held map **once per cycle**, over candidates
  WITHOUT a pane match (a pane match short-circuits and never probes), bounded by
  the existing per-tick cap (`HYDRATOR_MAX_ITEMS_PER_TICK`) and run as a bounded
  step under `HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- Cost discipline: no extra `wl`/`herdr` spawn per item; if the probe is
  unavailable/throws/times out, the cycle suppresses demotion for that tick and
  logs a named reason (fail-open, consistent with `pane-list` /
  `dep-list` handling) — never a release on ambiguous evidence.
- **Diagnosable log lines** (extend the existing hydrator log-format tests):
  `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder pid <pid> session <sid>` on
  suppression, and
  `[hydrator] released <id>: … (no pane, claim holder dead)` on release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Live claim holder suppresses demotion:** an `in-progress` item with **no** matching pane but whose `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is currently **held** (non-blocking `flock` fails with `EWOULDBLOCK`) is left untouched by the cycle (counted as skipped) and logs `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder pid <pid> session <sid>` — covered by an orchestration unit test over `runHydrationOnce` with a faked held verdict.
- [ ] **Dead holders are still released (no regression to stuck claims):** an item with no pane and a free lock whose recorded `pid` is not alive is demoted exactly as today (`open`/`intake_complete`) within one cycle, logging `[hydrator] released <id>: … (no pane, claim holder dead)`.
- [ ] **Diagnosable log lines:** every suppression and every release names the deciding signal, e.g. `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder pid <pid> session <sid>` and `[hydrator] released <id>: … (no pane, claim holder dead)` — the existing hydrator log-format tests are extended rather than replaced.
- [ ] **Existing decision branches are unchanged:** pane match ⇒ untouched; no lock file ⇒ demoted; active outbound dep blocker ⇒ `blocked`; stage `in_review` ⇒ `completed` — each covered by a test.
- [ ] **A held claim never overrides the `blocked`/`in_review` branches:** tests assert `held: true` still yields `blocked` (active dep) and `completed` (`in_review`), and that only the `open` release is suppressed.
- [ ] Pane-matched items never invoke the claim probe (test asserts zero probe calls for them).
- [ ] **Cost stays bounded:** a multi-item cycle performs one lock-directory read, no additional `wl`/`herdr` spawn per item, and keeps the batched dep-read fast path intact (test asserts the counts).
- [ ] A probe step timeout/throw suppresses demotion for that cycle with a named `[hydrator] … claim-probe` reason and does not demote anything (test).
- [ ] Changed-scope test gate green via `/skill:test` and `npm run build` clean.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `HydratorDeps` seam, `decideDemotion` context, `runHydrationOnce` cycle wiring, `createProductionHydratorDeps`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — decision cases, orchestration cases, log-format assertions, spawn/read counting.
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — the probe from the sibling child.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `getWorklogDir()` / `buildWlArgs()`.

## Out of scope

Release-path `assignee` clearing and the audit comment (sibling child); docs
rewrite (sibling child); dispatch, worklist marker, `implement.py` and the drive
orchestrator (explicitly out of the parent's scope).

# Release clears the scheduling hold and names the previous holder

Parent: WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY — *[bug] hydrator demotes in-progress claims of pane-less driven sessions (no matching pane)*.

Phase 3: the release-trail slice (parent AC7, producer decision Q3 = A). Depends
on *Busy = pane OR live claim holder (decision + cycle wiring)*.

## Goal (user story)

As a producer, a claim released by the hydrator must not stay parked on a
scheduling hold, and the release trail must say *who* held it — so a released item
is genuinely dispatchable again and the release is explicable from the item alone.

## Context the implementer must not re-derive

- Live evidence of the defect: `LP-0MVUH9OMY004MQ3U` sat at `open/intake_complete`
  with `assignee=Map` after its 04:36:31Z release, because `applyDemotion` passes
  only `--status`/`--stage`. A non-empty `assignee` is the scheduling hold
  (WL-0MV85WDOM007BKF8), so residue makes an item permanently undispatchable.
- Reuse, do not reinvent: `rollbackClaimWorkItem()` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
  already implements the same release shape — status/stage restore **plus**
  `--assignee ""` guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`, so a concurrent assignee
  change cannot be clobbered (audit-tier variant is status-neutral). Mirror that
  CAS shape rather than passing a bare `--assignee ""`.
- The audit-comment convention already exists for the downtime worker:
  `wl comment add <id> --comment <text> --author herdr-downtime --json` via
  `buildWlArgs*` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `recordDispatch`). The hydrator's
  author is `herdr-hydrator`.
- `wl list --status in-progress --json` already carries `assignee`, so the previous
  holder needs **no extra spawn**.

## What to build

- `HydratorItem` gains `assignee?: string`; `normaliseItem()` reads it.
- `applyDemotion` gains the previous holder (and, when useful, the deciding
  signal), e.g.
  `applyDemotion(itemId, status, stage, opts?: { previousAssignee?: string; reason?: string })`,
  and emits `wl update <id> --status <s> --stage <st> --assignee "" --if-assignee <prev> --json`
  when a previous holder is known (no `--if-assignee` guard when it is empty).
- A release audit comment per demotion:
  `wl comment add <id> --comment "<reason>; previous assignee: <holder|(none)>" --author herdr-hydrator --json`,
  e.g. `released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: implement`.
  Comment failure is tolerated (logged, cycle continues; the `[hydrator] released`
  log line remains the primary local trail) and must never abort the cycle or
  re-demote.
- Update existing `hydrator.test.ts` deps/typings for the new signature (the test
  file declares a `ContractDeps` interface that must stay in step).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Release clears the scheduling hold:** the demotion `wl update` argument vector includes `--assignee ""` and, when a previous holder is known, `--if-assignee <previous>` — asserted exactly in a test.
- [ ] The release audit comment body names the deciding signal and the previous holder (e.g. `released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: implement`), with `--author herdr-hydrator` — asserted in a test.

    item is busy."*), then add the **second** signal: a live per-child claim

# Verification: full suite green + live pane-less holder survives a real cycle

Parent: WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY — *[bug] hydrator demotes in-progress claims of pane-less driven sessions (no matching pane)*.

Phase 5: acceptance evidence. Depends on the probe, wiring, release-path and docs
children. This child exists because the defect was *observed in production* and
must be *observed fixed*, not only unit-tested.

## Goal (user story)

As the producer, I want the fix proven end-to-end against a real hydrator cycle so
I can trust that a live pane-less claim survives and an abandoned one still
self-heals — with the evidence captured on the work item.

## What to do

1. **Full suite + build gate.** `npm run build` at the repository root and the
   full test suite through the test skill (`/skill:test`); the dev-push gate is
   the enforcement point — no ad-hoc test invocations.
2. **Live pane-less holder dogfood (the defect, replayed):**
   - Create/choose a scratch work item in this store, claim it
     (`wl update <id> --status in-progress --assignee <agent>`) so the hydrator
     considers it, and take its child lock from a **process with no herdr pane**
     (e.g. a background `flock`/`work_item_lock.py` holder) — this reproduces a
     driven session without spawning a full one.
   - Watch `<this repo>/.worklog/logs/hydrator.log` across **≥ 3 cycles** (~90 s
     at `HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`): the item must stay `in-progress` and the log must
     show `[hydrator] kept <id>: live claim holder …` with **no**
     `released <id> … (no matching pane)` line for it.
   - Release the lock: within one cycle the item must be released
     (`open`/`intake_complete`), the log must carry the
     `released … (no pane, claim holder dead)` line, `wl show <id>` must report an
     **empty assignee**, and the release comment must name the previous holder
     (`--author herdr-hydrator`) — the live proof for the release-trail AC.
   - Clean up the scratch item and any lock file afterwards.
3. Record the evidence (log excerpt with timestamps, `wl show` before/after,
   commit SHAs) in a comment on this item and on the parent, then set the parent's
   stage to `in_review`.

## Operational preconditions (capture them if unmet)

The hydrator only runs inside a **visible** herdr worklist pane for this root
(visibility-gated). If no ContextHub worklist pane is visible during the run,
record that fact in a comment and fall back to driving `runHydrationOnce` against
the real store with production deps from an integration script (read-only apart
from the intended demotion of the scratch item) — do not weaken the evidence to
"unit tests pass".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run build` is clean at the repository root and the full test suite passes through `/skill:test` — **the full project test suite must pass with the new changes**.
- [ ] Live: a pane-less held claim survives ≥ 3 real hydrator cycles (log excerpt captured, item still `in-progress`).
- [ ] Live: after the holder exits, the item is released within one cycle, its `assignee` is empty, and the release comment names the previous holder.
- [ ] Live: a stale lock (free `flock`, dead pid) is still released within one cycle — no regression to stuck claims.
- [ ] Evidence (log excerpt, `wl show` before/after, commit hashes) recorded as a comment on this item **and** on the parent before the parent moves to `in_review`.
- [ ] Scratch item, lock files and any temporary script removed; `git status` clean in the worktree.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — the code under live test.
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — the probe under live test.
- `.worklog/logs/hydrator.log` — the live evidence sink (bounded, 200 lines).
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md` — the documented behaviour the evidence must match.

## Out of scope

New behaviour or refactoring; any fix found during verification is raised as its
own work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY`) unless it blocks this
verification.

Same-project `dep add`/`rm`/`list` output is byte-identical to today (regression).
- `wl dep add` accepts an id whose prefix belongs to a discovered sibling store:
  existence is validated against that store, and the edge is written to the
  **local** store with the foreign id as `toId`.

  foreign-target path (e.g. `addDependencyEdge(ctx, from, to, { allowForeignTarget: true })`)

  dependent, with no write to the foreign store.

## Summary

Make every dependency-blocker evaluation resolve foreign targets from their own
store, with an explicit fail-safe when the store is unavailable (D3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC traceability.** **AC3 — Gating.** An item whose only active blocker is a foreign item is excluded from `wl next` and included with `--include-blocked`; the same item becomes selectable once the foreign item reaches `in_review`/`done`/ `completed`/`deleted`; a removed sibling store leaves the item blocked with `unresolved: true` and a reason in JSON (never unblocked).
- `getActiveDependencyBlockers`, `hasActiveBlockers` and every `isDependencyActive`
  consumer resolve a foreign target's `status`/`stage` from its own store using
  the existing terminal semantics — the predicate is reused, not forked.
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` `buildEdgeCache` keeps foreign targets
  out of `itemsById`, and no resolver assumes a local row exists.
- `wl next` blocked-candidate filtering, `--include-blocked` and blocker surfacing
  (`next-pipeline.ts`) report foreign blockers with `unresolved` and a `reason`.
- `wl doctor` distinguishes an unresolved foreign edge (`severity: warning`,
  `foreign_dependency: unresolved`) from a genuinely missing local endpoint
  (the existing `dependency.missing-endpoint` error) — no false finding.
- Fail-safe: a foreign store that disappears mid-run leaves the dependent
  blocked and logs one warning; no unhandled exception, no silent unblock.
- An **ambiguous** foreign prefix is never resolved to one candidate: the blocker
  is reported `unresolved: true` with an `ambiguous` reason and stays blocking.
- The F5 gating spec passes.

- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — foreign resolution + fail-safe

## Summary

Implement `wl project add` (URL + clone + config mapping) and the
`unknown_project` error surface that replaces the bare `Work item not found`
(D4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC traceability.** **AC4 — Missing project remediation.** An unknown prefix produces `error_code: "unknown_project"` with the projects root and the exact `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url>` remediation; `wl project add` clones into the projects root, records the mapping, validates the prefix, and is idempotent; a prefix mismatch or clone failure exits non-zero without leaving a mapping behind; no stdin prompt without `--interactive`.
- `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url> [--path <dir>]` records
  `projects.<PREFIX>.path` (and the git URL) in `.worklog/config.yaml`, cloning
  with `git clone <url> <path>` only when the path does not exist.
- The cloned store's `config.yaml` prefix must match `PREFIX`; a mismatch exits
  non-zero with remediation and writes no mapping.
- A clone failure exits non-zero, leaves no mapping and no partial directory
  behind in the projects root.
- Re-running against an existing correct clone is a no-op (no clone, no duplicate
  mapping, exit 0).
- No stdin prompt by default; `--interactive` prompts for the URL only when
  `--git-url` is omitted. Git credentials come from the operator's existing git
  configuration — the tool never prompts for them.
- `wl dep add`, `wl dep list` and `wl next` return the `unknown_project` payload
  (`prefix`, `projects_root`, `remediation`) instead of a bare
  `Work item not found`.
- The F7 spec passes.

data.description:
Discovered while diagnosing local/remote routing for LP-0MVK6XGOF000C45C on
2026-10-31 (proxy-log-debug session). Proxy-side sibling defect is filed
separately in the llm store (see Related work).

## Summary

The downtime worker's local-capacity reservation client posts
`expected_tokens`, but `POST /llama/local/reserve` requires
`estimated_tokens`. The proxy answers `400 {"error":"estimated_tokens is
required"}`, `createLocalReserver` maps any non-2xx/non-429 response to `null`
(fail-open by design), and the dispatcher therefore launches the pane with **no
ticket and no capacity check**. The only dispatch-time local-capacity gate in the
worker is inert, and it fails silently — a dispatch record shows
`reservationTicketId: null, reservation: null` with no deferral reason.

## Problem statement

`buildLocalReservationRequest` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts:117-125`)
returns:

```ts
{ expected_tokens: DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS /* 8192 */,
  priority: 'background', cache_state: 'unknown' }
```

The proxy's handler (`proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:396-410`) reads only
`estimated_tokens`:

```python
raw_tokens = body.get("estimated_tokens")
if raw_tokens is None:
    return 400, {"error": "estimated_tokens is required", "admit": False}
```

Verified live against the running proxy (2026-10-31, read-only `dry_run`):

```
POST /llama/local/reserve {"expected_tokens":4000,…}
  → 400 {"error": "estimated_tokens is required", "admit": false}
POST /llama/local/reserve {"estimated_tokens":4000,…}
  → 200 {"admit": true, "dry_run": true, "reason": "within_budget",
          "projected_wait_s": 7.8, "budget_s": 60.0}
```

Consequence: `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts:295-330` documents
"refused (429) → DEFER with the proxy's retry_after_s, roll the claim back",
but an unusable *request* can never produce a refusal — only `null`, which the
code treats as "older proxy, fail open, dispatch anyway". The per-dispatch
capacity handshake (parent WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8, slice C2) is therefore dead
code in production, and the worker cannot distinguish "proxy too old" from
"our body is wrong".

Evidence from the live dispatch that exposed it
(`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, llm project, 2026-10-31T12:49:27Z):

```json
{ "itemId": "LP-0MVK6XGOF000C45C", "kind": "audit",
  "localPreference": "remote-ok", "localPreferenceReason": "default",
  "reservationTicketId": null, "reservation": null }
```

## Users

- **Primary user — the operator.** Believes dispatched work is admitted against
  real local capacity; in fact nothing is checked, so a burst of downtime panes
  can pile onto a 2-slot local pool (or, as on 2026-10-31, be launched
  `remote-ok` while nobody notices the gate never ran).
- **Secondary user — the next maintainer of the reservation handshake.** A
  silent 400/no-ticket loop makes the feature look "fail-open working" instead
  of "contract broken".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The request body the client builds uses the field the proxy contract
      requires (`estimated_tokens`) and a unit test pins the exact wire body
      against the documented proxy contract, so a rename on either side fails
      the test rather than degrading to `null`.
- [ ] A `429` refusal still defers the dispatch with the proxy's
      `retry_after_s`, rolls the claim back, and writes no success marker /
      spawn (existing C2 behaviour retained, asserted by test).
- [ ] Fail-open is preserved for genuinely unusable responses (`404`, `5xx`,
      timeout, unparseable body) — asserted by the existing tests, unchanged.
- [ ] An unusable-response outcome is **distinguishable from a refusal** in the
      dispatch record/log (e.g. a `reservationUnavailable`/probe-failure field
      or a log line naming the failing exchange), so a broken contract can never
      again look like an old proxy.
- [ ] End-to-end evidence recorded on this item: after the fix, a real downtime
      dispatch on this host records a non-null `reservationTicketId` when the
      proxy grants, and a deferral reason when it refuses (capture the
      `downtime-dispatches.log` entry in a comment).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes
      (`packages/herdr` suite plus the repo-wide suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the handshake fail-open: an older/absent proxy must still never block a
  dispatch.
- Do not change the pane locality policy (`remote-ok` default, `low`-priority
  rule) — that is deliberate and out of scope.
- No proxy changes in this repo; the proxy owns its own contract (sibling item).
- `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` is already dirty in this checkout from
  unrelated work — leave it alone.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts` — request builder
  (`buildLocalReservationRequest:117`) and the tolerant parser/client
  (`createLocalReserver`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `LocalReservationRequest`
  (`expected_tokens` at ~376).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — the reserve gate
  (~295–330) and the dispatch record fields.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` —
  `DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS` / `LOCAL_RESERVE_PATH`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` and the
  dispatch-claims tests — where the wire-body assertion and the
  refuse/rollback cases belong.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-31)

- `downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts:110` — `DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS = 8_192`;
  `:121` — `expected_tokens: DEFAULT_LOCAL_RESERVATION_EXPECTED_TOKENS`.
- `downtime-worker.types.ts:376` — `expected_tokens: number;`.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:398` — proxy requires `estimated_tokens`
  (introduced by LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL on the proxy side).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1474` — `downtimeDeps.reserveLocalCapacity = createLocalReserver(runSettings.downtimeProxyUrl);`
  so the client IS wired; only the wire body is wrong.
- No existing work item covers this: `wl search "reservation ticket
  expected_tokens mismatch"` → 0 results in the llm store; no matching item in
  this store either.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` — parent: atomic local-admission reservation handshake
  (slices C1/C2/C3).
- `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (llm store) — proxy side of the handshake; defines
  `estimated_tokens` and the 429 refusal contract.
- `WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX` / `WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1` — pane locality preference
  (`remote-ok` default), the reason this defect stayed invisible: panes go
  remote anyway, so nobody missed the missing ticket.
- llm-store sibling item — "measured-cache-deficit 503 quarantines the whole
  local entry", the other defect found in the same diagnosis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — other clients of `/llama/local/reserve`.** Check for a second caller
  (e.g. the pi Worklog extension) before changing only this one; the fix should
  make the wire contract single-sourced if more than one caller exists.
- **Risk — proxy-side tolerance masking it again.** If the proxy ever accepts
  `expected_tokens` as an alias, this bug becomes invisible again; the
  acceptance evidence in AC5 pins the behaviour end-to-end instead of relying on
  reading code.
- **Assumption.** The proxy's `estimated_tokens` name is the intended contract
  (documented in `admission_reserve.py` and exercised by the live 200/400
  responses). If the proxy side is judged the one to change, coordinate with the
  sibling llm item rather than diverging.

## Review update (2026-10-31, follow-up diagnosis)

The wire-body mismatch is confirmed, and a second independent gap was found while
tracing the same window: **even with the body fixed, the ticket cannot protect the
local capacity this dispatch actually needs.**

Facts established from the proxy log and the code:

- Ticket TTL is `DEFAULT_RESERVE_TTL_SECONDS = 10` (max 60)
  (`llm/proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:52-53`), and the ticket reaches only the
  **pane** process via `PI_LOCAL_RESERVATION_TICKET` — the extension at
  `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts:63` is what turns it
  into the `X-Local-Reservation` header.
- A downtime audit dispatch runs its own agent loop with
  `localPreference: remote-ok` (medium priority ⇒ `default`), so its first request
  goes **remote** and the granted ticket is never consumed — the proxy already tracks
  these as reserved-but-unused (`admission_reserve.py` `stats()`:
  `reserved_issued` / `reserved_used` / `reserved_expired`, exposed through the
  `/llama/local/status` payload at `proxy/proxy/handlers.py:1054`).
- The process that *does* need local capacity is the audit runner's own `pi`
  subprocess (`audit-LP-…-parent-…`, `prefer-local`). It starts ~12 minutes after the
  dispatch and runs `pi --no-context-files --no-skills --no-extensions`
  (`audit_runner.py:4593`), so it cannot send `X-Local-Reservation` even though it
  inherits the env var — and the 10 s TTL expired long before.
- Observed consequence in the same window: dispatch `12:28:50` (proxy reported
  `available_slots=2 capacity_hint=idle`); the audit's first local attempt at
  `12:40:05` succeeded once, then `12:41:13 local_dispatch_denied` (slot owned by
  another session) → `fallback_after_queue` → remote. Final tally for that audit
  subprocess: **1 local / 7 remote streams**.

So fixing AC1 alone would leave the dispatch record looking healthy
(`reservationTicketId` non-null, AC5 evidence green) while local utilisation stays
near zero — the "green but unmet" outcome this item exists to prevent.

### Additional acceptance criteria (from the review)

- [ ] **AC7 — The reservation must have a real beneficiary.** Assert end-to-end that
      a granted ticket is consumed by the request it was granted for (proxy
      `/llama/local/status` reservation counters show `reserved_used ≥ 1` and
      `reserved_outstanding` returns to 0 for the dispatch), **or** that no ticket is
      requested when the dispatched session cannot consume local capacity. The chosen
      rule is documented on this item with its rationale and pinned by a test.
- [ ] **AC8 — No reserved-but-unused tickets for downtime panes.** A `remote-ok`
      dispatch (the default for every non-`low` priority candidate,
      `DOWNTIME_LOCAL_PREFERENCE`) must not reserve local capacity it will never use:
      either skip the reserve call for such dispatches and record that decision in the
      dispatch record, or reserve for the process that will consume it. A dispatch
      record must never show both `reservationTicketId != null` and a session that
      issues no local request.
- [ ] **AC9 — Bound and document the TTL / beneficiary limitation.** Record on this
      item and in `downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`'s docstring that the ticket
      TTL is 10 s and that only the pane's own first request can consume it; if a
      local-consuming child process (audit runner, or any `--no-extensions` session)
      is ever expected to use a ticket, either raise the TTL for that path or have the
      child take its own reservation — silently relying on an expired ticket is not
      acceptable. Asserted by a test that a ticket older than the TTL is not treated
      as capacity by the client.

## Review update #2 (2026-10-31, proxy-log review — llm session `herdr-1793450762-1330301-22426`)

### Independent confirmation from the proxy side

- The dispatch record for the audit in the reviewed window shows exactly the state this
  item describes: `localPreference: "remote-ok"`, `localPreferenceReason: "default"`,
  `reservationTicketId: null`, `reservation: null` — and **no** deferral/unavailable
  marker, so the record cannot tell "policy" from "broken client".
- The proxy side of the pair is confirmed too: `/llama/local/status` reported
  `available_slots=2 capacity_hint=idle llama_server_running=true` for the whole
  pre-dispatch window (12:44–12:46), and the dispatched audit nevertheless ran
  **45/45 requests and 37/37 streams remote** — because the local entry was in a
  repeating 60 s cooldown armed by another session's measured-cache aborts
  (llm-store sibling LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ, AC1/AC10/AC11 now cover the proxy fix).
- So the two defects compose exactly as the "Review update" says: the wire-body fix
  (AC1) would have produced a *successful* reservation for a local capacity this
  dispatch could never use, and the ticket counters would have looked healthy.

### The trap in AC7/AC8 option (a) — record it before implementing

AC8 permits "skip the reserve call for `remote-ok` dispatches and record that decision".
Taken **alone**, that makes *no ticket* the documented norm for every non-`low` priority
candidate, and the ticket disappears as a health signal entirely: a dispatch record that
never had a ticket looks identical whether the run used 100 % local or 100 % remote. The
operator's real question ("did my unattended work actually use the GPU I paid for?") then
has no answer in this repo. Hence AC10 — it is the outcome-level counterpart to the
proxy-side status fields, and it is what makes option (a) safe.

### Additional acceptance criterion

- [ ] **AC10 — record the observed routing outcome, so a green dispatch record cannot
      hide a 0 %-local run.** Every dispatch record (or the same `downtime-dispatches`
      entry, written when the pane's work window closes) carries the **observed** split
      for the dispatched session: `localStreams` and `remoteStreams` (or an equivalent
      `localShare`), sourced from the bounded route log / proxy session attribution —
      never from the reservation ticket. A dispatch whose session issued requests and
      consumed **0 local** capacity is recorded with an explicit `localStarved: true`,
      and when the dispatched work is `prefer-local` (e.g. an audit whose runner
      subprocess is `prefer-local`) a WARNING line names the dispatch, the split and the
      proxy's `local_route_reason` if available. Tests: a stub route log producing
      0 local / 7 remote yields `localStarved: true` with the split recorded; a
      mixed 3/4 split yields `localStarved: false`; a dispatch with no requests at all
      is recorded as `notObserved` (never as healthy). Rationale: AC7/AC8 may legitimately
      remove the ticket — the observed outcome must take over as the capacity-health
      signal, otherwise this item's own "end-to-end evidence" (AC5) can pass while local
      utilisation is ~0, which is the failure mode that motivated the review update.

### Planning note for whoever picks this up

AC10 was added after `plan_complete`; the plan's task breakdown needs one line for it
(record the outcome from the route log at window close + the stub-log tests). No other
AC changes: AC1–AC9 stand as written.

## Problem

`packages/herdr` postbuild (`scripts/install-herdr.sh`) runs `npm ci` in the **main checkout** even when the build itself runs inside a linked worktree (`npm run build` in `.worklog/worktrees/<wl-...>`). `npm ci` deletes `node_modules`, which removes the workspace link `packages/herdr/node_modules/@worklog/shared -> ../../../shared` and replaces it with an **empty real directory**.

Every consumer of `@worklog/shared/*` inside the worktree then fails to resolve (the whole `packages/herdr/node_modules` tree is symlinked from the main checkout, so the damage is shared). Symptom observed: `implement.py finish`'s gate reported 113 failing CLI tests whose only error was empty stdout (`expected '' to contain '"success": false"'`) — the CLI could not start.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `install-herdr.sh` (or the postbuild step) only installs when the resolved checkout is the repository root, never for a linked worktree build; a worktree build reuses the main checkout's installed dependencies.
2. When `npm ci` does run, the `@worklog/shared` workspace link is restored by the same step (as `link-shared.mjs` already does) so a wiped link can never survive a build.
3. A regression test asserts that building in a linked worktree leaves `packages/herdr/node_modules/@worklog/shared` resolving to the live workspace package.
4. `implement.py finish` in a fresh worktree keeps the full suite green (no empty-stdout CLI failures).

## Evidence

Discovered while finishing WL-0MVV1F1P1005PO5M (leaf-aware audit dispatch C6). Recovered by `node packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs`. Earlier in the same session a related wipe removed `packages/shared/dist`, making `wl` itself unrunnable ("the shared workspace build output is missing").

## Mechanism (verified during planning)

1. `scripts/install-herdr.sh` deliberately resolves `REPO_ROOT` to the **first** `git worktree list --porcelain` entry — the main checkout — even when invoked from a linked worktree (WL-0MSRG481O007QVEA). `HERDR_DIR` is therefore `<main>/packages/herdr`.
2. Step 0 (`npm ci --prefix "${HERDR_DIR}"`, WL-0MSRLH52R003CK49) wipes and reinstalls the main checkout's `packages/herdr/node_modules`.
3. Worktree creation in the implement skill symlinks `<worktree>/packages/herdr/node_modules` -> `<main>/packages/herdr/node_modules` (and the repo-root `node_modules`), so the wipe propagates into every live worktree.
4. Step 0b (`node link-shared.mjs "${HERDR_DIR}"`, WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q) repairs the main checkout link, but only after `npm ci` has already destroyed it — any run that fails or is interrupted between steps 0 and 0b leaves the link wiped, and the worktree never runs the install/link itself.

Design consequence: the dependency install is redundant for a worktree build (the worktree consumes the main checkout's `node_modules` through the symlink), which is exactly what AC1 asks for.

## Scope note (clarification of AC1, no intent change)

AC1 governs the **dependency-install** step (step 0) only. The `herdr plugin link` step must keep targeting the main checkout from a worktree build (WL-0MSRG481O007QVEA) — a worktree-based plugin link dangles once `implement.py finish` deletes the worktree. Implementations must not turn the whole script into a no-op under a worktree.

## Reuse / related work

- `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` already exports `linkSharedPackage()` / `resolveSharedLinkTarget()` and is idempotent + fail-open — reuse it rather than writing new linking logic.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` already wires `postinstall` -> `node ./scripts/link-shared.mjs`, so an `npm ci` in the herdr package re-links on success; the gap is that the install runs against the wrong checkout and the failure window is unguarded.
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` already has a real-git worktree scenario (`links the plugin from the main checkout when run inside a linked worktree`, using `realGitBin()`), which is the natural place to extend for AC3.
- `tests/unit/link-shared.test.ts` covers `linkSharedPackage()` behaviour.
- `_ensure_node_modules_symlink()` / `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks()` in the implement skill are the symlink creators — useful evidence for AC3/AC4, not to be modified from this item.
- Distinct from WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG (implement finish wiped tracked `packages/shared` files) — different root cause, no overlap.

## Key Files

- `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs`
- `packages/herdr/package.json`
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`
- `tests/unit/link-shared.test.ts`

# Recurrence: `packages/shared` wiped from the main checkout (2026-10-31) — wl broken machine-wide

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Status source:** AH-0MVVNKP1B00701HR

## Problem statement

For the second time in five days (previous: 2026-10-26, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG),
a concurrent, worktree-scoped agent run deleted every tracked file under
`packages/shared/` from the main ContextHub checkout, plus the gitignored
`packages/shared/dist/` build output. Because `wl` resolves
`@worklog/shared/worklog-paths` from that build output, **every `wl`
invocation on the machine failed for ~35 minutes** until an AI_Hell session
repaired it, blocking every agent in ContextHub, AI_Hell and
any other project using the shared `wl` CLI. The 2026-10-26 hardening (the
finish main-checkout guard + `guarded_run_all`, shipped in v1.0.24) did **not**
prevent this event, so the guard's coverage must be re-examined rather than
re-applied.

## Users

- **All agents on the host** (ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, …) — `wl` is the
  single source of truth for work tracking; a broken `wl` fails closed for
  every agent machine-wide.
  - *User story:* "As an agent finishing a work item, I want the main checkout
    protected from foreign deletions, so that my `wl` commands never die with
    'the shared workspace build output is missing'."
- **The developer/operator (producer)** — must be able to recover in one step
  and to trust `finish`'s guard report.
  - *User story:* "As an operator, I want a one-command recovery and a loud,
    named cause, so a wipe never costs 35 minutes of machine-wide downtime."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Forensic determination recorded.** A written timeline and actor
  determination for the 2026-10-31 wipe live in this item's description:
  who/what deleted `packages/shared`, with evidence. Where the actor cannot be
  proven after the fact, the item records what was ruled out and names the
  residual hypothesis (precedent: WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG AC1).
- **AC2 — ContextHub-side integrity check.** A check that runs independently of
  `implement.py finish` (e.g. `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` or a new
  `scripts/check-main-checkout.sh`) detects tracked-file deletions in the main
  checkout and fails loudly, naming every deleted path and the concurrent
  actor evidence — so deletions are reported even when the overlapping finish
  run aborts at the test gate (the 2026-10-31 run's `verifies: []` gap).
  Covered by a regression test.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic fires on this exact state.** `wl`'s missing-shared-dist
  diagnostic is confirmed (test) to fire when tracked sources *and* `dist/`
  are gone, and its remediation text covers both `git restore`/`git checkout`
  for deleted tracked files and `npm run build:shared` for the gitignored
  output.
- **AC4 — One-step recovery.** A runbook exists in `docs/dev/` restoring
  `packages/shared` from git + `npm run build:shared`, **and** a
  `scripts/repair-shared-package.sh` (producer decision: Option B) performs
  the restore in one command — deleted tracked files from HEAD, then `dist/`
  rebuild — with a smoke test.
- **AC5 — Validation.** Regression tests cover AC2–AC4 (AC1 is a written
  forensic record, validated by review rather than by a test); all related
  documentation (this item's runbook, `docs/dev/wl-shared-dist-diagnostic.md`,
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, code comments) is updated to reflect the
  changes; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

> **Moved to SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM (producer decision, Option C):** the
> `implement.py` finish-guard hardening (failure-path verification +
> cross-checkout attribution) ships in the SorraAgents repo under that item.
> This item tracks the ContextHub-side deliverables (AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5) and
> cross-references it; the SorraAgents item cross-references this one.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundaries.** `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` lives in
  the SorraAgents repo (`~/projects/SorraAgents`). The producer authorises the
  guard changes there under **SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM** (linked work item); this
  item makes no agent-infrastructure edits.
- **No weakening of existing guards.** The 2026-10-26 main-checkout guard
  (fail-loud on deletions, `own_churn` allow-list, single-owner finish lock)
  and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` invariants must stay intact.
- **Non-destructive recovery.** Restoring from git must never stash, reset or

Evidence sources: `.worklog/logs/finish-child4d.log` (the overlapping finish
run for WL-0MVTVZHFU000PRT6), the gate test-slot timing, `packages/shared`
file mtimes and `git reflog`. The evidence is partially destroyed (the repair
restored files from git, rewriting mtimes), so the ruling-out bar follows the
WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG precedent: conclusive proof only where the evidence
permits; otherwise the residual hypothesis below.

### Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-31)

| Time | Event | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 14:43:06 | Finish gate starts for WL-0MVTVZHFU000PRT6: `main_checkout_guard` snapshot taken in `finish-child4d.log` — `baseline_paths: 2` (the two staged regression tests), `own_churn: []`, **`verifies: []`** | `finish-child4d.log` guard JSON |

| 14:58 | Run aborted at the gate — **no guard verify point was reached**, so `verifies: []` and nothing reported the 37 deletions. This reporting gap is what AC2 closes | `finish-child4d.log` report |

A **concurrent, worktree-scoped agent run other than the finish run**

gitignored `dist/` — a whole-directory removal, unlike the 2026-10-26
rimraf-dist-only shape). Timing places the wipe at ≈14:53 — the exact minute

independent of a finish run that may abort at the gate) and in

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts > install-herdr script > migrates a legacy open-worklist binding in-place to the new action
- Failing commit: c3f2daa5
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Error: Test timed out in 30000ms (tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts:180). Observed at 2026-10-31T13:27Z under host load average 30-43 with ~41 concurrent run_tests waiters; the same test passed on the next fresh full-suite run at 2026-10-31T15:29Z (4173 passed / 5 skipped). The test spawns scripts/install-herdr.sh, which runs `npm ci` in packages/herdr — in a worktree that writes through the node_modules symlink into the shared main checkout, so concurrent agent builds make it exceed the 30s timeout.
```

## Root Cause (investigated during planning)

**Environmental, load-induced timeout — not a product regression.** Mechanism verified against the current `dev` sources:

1. The failing test spawns `scripts/install-herdr.sh` with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (`tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`, `runScript` helper), so `npm` resolves to `/usr/bin/npm` and IS on PATH.
2. `install-herdr.sh` resolves `REPO_ROOT` to the **main checkout** (first `git worktree list --porcelain` entry, worktree-safe resolution for WL-0MSRG481O007QVEA) and, in step 0, runs `npm ci --prefix <main-checkout>/packages/herdr`.
3. Worktrees created by `implement.py` symlink `packages/herdr/node_modules` (and repo-root `node_modules`) into the main checkout, so that install is shared across concurrent agent builds.
4. Under heavy host load (load average 30-43, ~41 concurrent `run_tests` waiters) the `npm ci` step exceeded the global `testTimeout: 30000` in `vitest.config.ts`, producing the observed `Test timed out in 30000ms`.
5. The same test passed on the next fresh full-suite run (2026-10-31T15:29Z, 4173 passed / 5 skipped), confirming flakiness rather than a deterministic defect.

The underlying shared-checkout mechanism is tracked separately in **WL-0MVWJ4IKT005SAHT** (worktree postbuild `npm ci` wipes the `@worklog/shared` workspace link) and **WL-0MVMZLC410001BP9** (worktree module-resolution isolation docs). This item is the flaky-timeout symptom; the triage determination is **flaky**, per the triage runbook (`skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`).

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the latest `dev` (failure observed at commit `c3f2daa5`).
2. Run the failing test — note it is a **vitest** test, not pytest (corrected during planning):
   `npx vitest run tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts -t 'migrates a legacy open-worklist binding in-place to the new action'`
   or via the canonical runner: `python3 $(skill_path test)/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full`
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

On an idle host the test passes; the timeout reproduces only under concurrent host load (many parallel builds/test runs sharing the main checkout's `packages/herdr/node_modules`).

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item. Flaky and load-dependent, so the practical impact is intermittent red suites, not a deterministic failure.

## Candidate Remediations (for implementation)

- **A — Explicit per-test timeout (preferred):** give the install-herdr subprocess tests an explicit `{ timeout }` of 45-60 s, matching the guidance already documented in `vitest.config.ts` ("Tests that spawn tsx subprocesses should set explicit per-test timeouts (45-60s) since subprocess startup is slow under concurrent load").
- **B — Hermetic migration test:** place a fake `npm` earlier on the test's `PATH` so `install-herdr.sh` step 0 skips the real `npm ci`; the test then verifies keybinding migration in isolation, with no shared-checkout side effect.
- **C — Both:** explicit timeout as a safety net plus hermetic `npm` stub to remove the shared-checkout side effect entirely.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once (done during planning — passed on the 2026-10-31T15:29Z fresh run; the 13:27Z failure was a load-induced 30 s timeout).
2. If reproducible under normal load, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue (applied during planning).

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts > install-herdr script > migrates a legacy open-worklist binding in-place to the new action` passes against the latest `dev` and no longer times out under concurrent host load (no 30 s `testTimeout` violation).
2. A remediation from the candidate list is chosen and documented on this item, preventing recurrence (explicit per-test timeout and/or a hermetic test that does not run a real `npm ci`).
3. Any documentation that describes the install-herdr tests' runtime/timing expectations (e.g. `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`, `vitest.config.ts` comments) is updated to reflect the remediation, or a comment on this item records explicitly that no documentation change is required.
4. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVWJ4IKT005SAHT** (open) — herdr postbuild `npm ci` in a worktree build wipes the `@worklog/shared` workspace link; the shared-checkout `npm ci` mechanism that causes this timeout. Does not make this item a duplicate: it does not cover the timeout/flakiness of the migration test itself.
- **WL-0MVMZLC410001BP9** (open) — Document worktree module-resolution isolation (docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md).
- **WL-0MSG6O6Z5005DAZV / WL-0MSG6OA2K003GY27** (completed) — original install-herdr tests/script.

## Key Files

- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`
- `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
- `vitest.config.ts`
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

# Reduce per-command production startup cost (re-scoped from WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost
**Decision source:** child 1 profile (WL-0MVVXFXM6007QZ2L, commit ebde3586) + child 3 decision gate (WL-0MVVXG4B200968BF).

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want a warm CLI invocation against an already-initialised store
to skip the per-call SQLite schema/migration bootstrap and YAML config re-parse,
so the ~2.2 ms (47 %) of every data-access call that is startup work stops being
paid again on each invocation — in the test suite's ~1200 in-process calls and in
real operator use.

## Context

Measured attribution (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` § 'In-process CLI harness
cost', `bench/inproc-harness-profile.json`), median of 5, fresh temp store:

| scenario | total | db open (schema+migrations) | config load | harness-side |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wl list --json` | 4.7 ms | 2.2 ms (47.3 %) | 0.0 ms | 1.5 ms (32.5 %) |
| `wl status` | 4.0 ms | 1.8 ms (44.8 %) | 0.2 ms (5.0 %) | 1.0 ms (25.4 %) |
| `wl create` | 5.1 ms | 2.1 ms (42.1 %) | 0.2 ms (3.8 %) | 0.8 ms (16.2 %) |

`getDatabase()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) calls `loadConfigRelaxed()` — which reads and
`yaml.load`s the config files — and then constructs `WorklogDatabase`
(`src/database.ts` → `packages/shared/src/database.ts`), which builds a
`SqlitePersistentStore` and runs the schema/migration bootstrap on every open.
This is production behaviour (not a test-harness artefact), so the fix belongs in
`src/`/`packages/shared` rather than in `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening an already-migrated store at the current schema version does **not**
  re-run the full migration scan on every open: the fast path is detected by a
  cheap schema-version comparison (e.g. `PRAGMA user_version` / a version table),
  and the slow path is still taken for a new, older, or partially-migrated store.
- Config load is not repeated needlessly within one process when the config files
  have not changed (cache keyed on the resolved config file paths plus their
  mtime/size or content hash), and the cache is invalidated when a file changes.
- Behaviour is unchanged: the full test suite passes with the same test counts,
  and schema-creation/migration/integrity tests are green (including downgrade
  and partial-migration cases).
- Median `wl list --json` warm per-call cost against a fresh temp store drops by
  **>= 30 %** versus the child 1 baseline (4.7 ms → <= 3.3 ms), measured on the
  same host as the median of >= 5 runs with load average quoted, using
  `npm run benchmark:inproc-harness -- --runs 5` (a bench script, never an
  ad-hoc vitest invocation).
- `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` (WL-0MVVXG3UW00250V5) is regenerated for the
  improved numbers and its guard test still passes; the before/after medians and
  the host load are recorded on this item.
- No test-harness workaround is introduced: `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` keeps
  constructing a database per call, so the saving is real production saving.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — store open + schema/migration bootstrap.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` construction/open path.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `getDatabase` (calls `loadConfigRelaxed` per call).
- `src/config.ts` — `loadConfig` / `loadConfigRelaxed` YAML parse.
- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts`, `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` — measurement.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — record the before/after numbers.

## Notes

- The migration path must stay obviously correct: a missed migration is data
  corruption, so the fast path must be conservatively gated and covered by tests
  that start from a real older schema.
- Any per-process config cache must be invalidated on file change; tests must
  exercise that invalidation (edit the config between two calls in one process).
